games.title: Cobra Command
games.alsoOn: Saturn & PS1 (JP, 'Thunder Storm & Road Blaster' set)
games.hook: Data East's 1984 helicopter laserdisc game, and the Sega CD port is the one everybody says is the best version it ever got.
games.cheats: Invincibility: at the main menu press Left, Right, A+B+C (a sound confirms), then B, A, C, A, Left, Left, Right, Left. Level select: press Start at the title, then Up, Left, Right, Right, Up when Game Start / Config Mode appear; an explosion confirms, then Left/Right on 'New York - Stage 1' picks the start stage. (FMV World)
games.video: Near full-screen window, ~15 fps, heavily dithered; among the better-looking Sega CD video for 1992.
games.difficulty: Medium — prompts are visible on screen; memorization over 6 stages.
games.trivia: Wolf Team handled the port; Renovation/Sega shipped it within the console's first months in the US. Anime work by Toei Animation.
games.variants: US (Sega), JP 'Thunder Storm FX' (Wolf Team). JP disc is more expensive.
games.notes: 1984 Data East laserdisc game. Helicopter QTE action; same style as Road Avenger. Sega CD port widely considered the best home version.

games.title: Road Avenger
games.hook: The one Sega CD laserdisc port people actually recommend: a Mad Max car-chase cartoon with an absurd synth soundtrack.
games.cheats: In the Options menu highlight 'Players', then: A six times = level select; C five times = debug mode (A+B+C during play); A five times then B = demo mode; A four times then B = pause enabled. (FMV World)
games.video: Near full-screen, ~15 fps, strong colors; one of the best-looking Sega CD FMV games.
games.difficulty: Medium-hard — fast directional prompts; later stages require memorization.
games.trivia: Data East's 1985 'Road Blaster' arcade game; Wolf Team port. The soundtrack was re-recorded for the Sega CD version and is a fan favourite.
games.variants: US (Renovation), EU (Sega), JP 'Road Blaster FX' (Wolf Team).
games.notes: 1985 Data East laserdisc game. Car-chase QTE; one of the best-regarded Sega CD FMV titles.

games.title: Time Gal
games.alsoOn: Saturn & PS1 (JP, 'Time Gal & Ninja Hayate' set)
games.hook: Taito's 1985 time-travelling heroine, never released in English, and the only laserdisc port on the console where the prompts are in Japanese.
games.cheats: Level select: at the main menu press Left, Right, Right, Up, then choose Game Start to pick level, area and screen orientation. GameFAQs also lists the correct inputs to clear every era and scene-viewer passwords (e.g. 1588 AD DRXHTLQJ). (GameFAQs)
games.video: Near full-screen, ~15 fps, slightly washed-out.
games.difficulty: Medium — includes 'Time Stop' multiple-choice sections that are pure trial and error.
games.endings: Single ending; 16 time periods in fixed order.
games.trivia: Animation by Toei. The Sega CD version was Wolf Team's first laserdisc port; it later shipped on Saturn/PS1 paired with Ninja Hayate.
games.variants: JP (Wolf Team, 13 Nov 1992), US (Renovation, 1993) and EU (Sega) releases; the international versions differ from the Japanese one (TCRF). Sega Retro could not be fetched from the cloud to confirm the US/EU dates (verify).
games.modern: No (Sega CD); arcade HD remaster in Taito LD Game Collection (Switch JP, 2023) and on Steam (2025).
games.notes: 1985 Taito laserdisc game. Japan only; menu text is Japanese but gameplay is prompt-based and playable without reading.
games.wherePlay: Original Sega CD disc on hardware or an emulator; arcade HD remaster sold separately on Switch and Steam.

games.title: Revenge of the Ninja
games.hook: The forgotten fourth laserdisc port: a Taito ninja cartoon so obscure most Sega CD collectors have never seen it running.
games.cheats: At the title with Game Start showing: Down, Left, Up, Right, Up, Right, Down, Left = stage select; Right, Left, Down, Up, Up, Down, Left, Right = infinite lives. Main menu Down, Down, Right, Up, then pause and press C to clear a level. Start screen Right, Left, Up, Down, Right, Left, Up = test mode with every cinematic. (GameFAQs)
games.video: Near full-screen, ~15 fps; animation quality is a step below Time Gal.
games.difficulty: Hard — short reaction windows and little on-screen prompting.
games.trivia: Arcade original 'Ninja Hayate' (1984). Renovation's US release was tiny, which is why it's rarer than the JP disc.
games.modern: No (Sega CD); arcade HD remaster in Taito LD Game Collection (Switch JP, 2023) and on Steam (2025).
games.notes: 1984 Taito laserdisc game. Did get a North American release via Renovation (corrects earlier note that it was JP-only).
games.wherePlay: Original Sega CD disc on hardware or an emulator; arcade HD remaster sold separately on Switch and Steam.

games.title: Dragon's Lair
games.alsoOn: CD-i, 3DO, Jaguar CD, PC, every modern platform
games.cast: Don Bluth animation
games.hook: The most famous FMV game ever made, in what might be its ugliest port — a perfect 'how bad can it get' episode.
games.cheats: Options set lives and difficulty; later difficulty levels add scenes, and there's no move indicator. View every scene: lose all lives, then press Right, Right, Left, Left, Down, Down, Up, Up and Start to continue; the lives counter stays at five and the game plays each sequence. (GameFAQs)
games.video: Small, low-res, extremely compressed window; widely called the worst-looking version of the game.
games.difficulty: Hard on Sega CD specifically — no move hints and sluggish input timing.
games.endings: Single ending; room order is semi-random.
games.trivia: ReadySoft's port reuses their PC/Mac CD-ROM conversion. The Sega CD's 64-colour video limit hits Bluth's animation harder than almost any other game.
games.variants: US and PAL (ReadySoft). PAL box is cardboard-style in some regions (verify).
games.modern: Yes (Dragon's Lair Trilogy on every current platform)
games.notes: Sega CD port has heavily compressed, low-res video and no on-screen prompts; often ranked among the weakest home ports of the game.

games.title: Space Ace
games.alsoOn: CD-i, 3DO, Jaguar CD, PC, modern platforms
games.cast: Don Bluth animation
games.hook: Dragon's Lair's sci-fi sibling, and the one where you can at least choose to stay small and weak for a different path.
games.cheats: Skill levels (Cadet, Captain, Space Ace) change how many scenes you play. View the video sequences: pause, then Right, Right, Left, Left, Down, Down, Up, Up, Start. (FMV World)
games.video: Same engine as Dragon's Lair: small, muddy window.
games.difficulty: Hard; the 'Energize' branching gives two paths per scene.
games.endings: Single ending with branching mid-scenes (Dexter vs. Ace paths).
games.trivia: Same ReadySoft tech; shipped after the console's peak so it sold poorly, hence the higher price today.
games.notes: Same ReadySoft engine and video quality as the Dragon's Lair port.

shots.title: All 4 of the floppy disks for the Atari ST version of the game 'Space Ace' taken using Cannon Power Shot S3

games.title: Panic!
games.hook: Data East made a game where every button does something ridiculous, and that's the whole game — the Sega CD's weirdest release.
games.cheats: No fail state, so no cheats needed. Scene select: at the title press Right, Right, Down, Up, Left, Right, Up, Up, Left, Down; scene 411 is a hidden attract demo. (GameFAQs)
games.video: Full-screen hand-drawn animation played through the Sega CD; smooth, very colourful.
games.endings: Multiple endings depending on which route reaches the central computer; dozens of branching rooms.
games.trivia: Titled 'Switch' in Japan; one of the few games where pressing the wrong button is the point. Hundreds of unique gag animations.
games.variants: US 'Panic!' (Sega), JP 'Switch' (Sega). US copies are scarcer and pricier.
games.notes: Hand-animated gag reels triggered by pressing buttons; not technically a laserdisc port but plays like one. JP release 1993, NA 1994.

games.title: Night Trap
games.source: Original; shot 1987 for the Hasbro NEMO console
games.cast: Dana Plato
games.cidTrigger: Theme song (Sunny Blaze)
games.length: 30 min per run; 1–2 hr to beat
games.hook: The game that got Congress involved, that is somehow also a slow surveillance puzzle about teen sleepover vampires.
games.cheats: No level or debug codes. Hidden video: during the end credits, when 'In Memory of Stephen D. Hassenfeld' appears, press Up then A five times. FMV World has a full room-and-time capture walkthrough. The 25th Anniversary edition adds a Theatre mode.
games.video: Small window (~1/4 screen), 64 colours, ~10 fps; the archetypal 'grainy Sega CD video'.
games.difficulty: Medium — mostly memorizing a trap timing schedule.
games.endings: One true ending plus several 'game over' sequences (each room's trap failures, Mr. Martin's warnings).
games.trivia: Shot in 1987 for Hasbro's cancelled 'Control-Vision' VHS console; budget ~$1.5M. Dana Plato's final notable role. Pulled from shelves in 1993 after the Senate hearings.
games.variants: Original 1992 box, 1993 'Red' re-release box, 32X CD (2 discs), Limited Run 2017/2018 reprints (Sega CD, 32X, premium editions). PriceCharting prices each separately.
games.modern: Yes (Night Trap 25th Anniversary — PS4, Switch, Xbox, PC)
games.notes: The game that triggered the 1993 US Senate hearings. Later 32X CD and 2017 25th Anniversary re-release.

games.title: Sewer Shark
games.cast: Robert Costanzo, David Underwood
games.hook: Can I shoot sewer monsters, remember the next turn and survive Ghost's performance reviews at the same time?
games.cheats: Continue: after reaching the Exterminator or Beach Bum level, lose and press A+C+Start as the credits begin to resume at the last level (later pressings: Start at the credits after Ratbreath). Taking three left (9) turns at the very start doesn't kill you. Track 2 on an audio CD player has a hidden 'Hello, Digital Pictures' message. (FMV World)
games.video: Larger video presentation on 3DO according to Digital Press; no dimensions or frame rate measured here. Do not describe either edition as full-screen without checking the actual presentation.
games.difficulty: Medium-hard — route memorization, instant death on missed turns.
games.endings: Single ending ('Solar City'); a 'bad' outcome if you fail the final run.
games.trivia: In Tristan Donovan's interview, Rob Fulop recalls filming the ending in Hawaii while discussing the expense of Hasbro's cancelled NEMO project.
games.variants: Sega CD is the Season Zero choice. Digital Press reports cleaner, larger 3DO video and changed sound effects, but less dependable targeting and diagonal input. These are attributed observations; compare the same scene before declaring a winner. Pressing-specific continue behavior remains unverified.
games.notes: Season Zero episode proposal: open on a missed turn, explain A firing / B steering mode / C hydrogen flares from the manual, then show practice and a timed attempt. Capture readable turn arrows, gauges and spoken directions. Optional 3DO comparison: match scene, enemy sounds and controller. The deliberate-low-score speedrun strategy still needs route evidence. Sources: https://www.segakore.fr/media/segakore/downloads/jeux/megacd/mcd_sewer_shark_bundle_manual_u.pdf https://www.digitpress.com/reviews/sewershark.htm https://www.gamedeveloper.com/business/the-replay-interviews-rob-fulop

Models, cables, audio routing and recording settings remain to be logged. Use the short and sustained capture checks in docs/season-zero-briefs.md before a full attempt.

games.cast: Corey Haim, Debbie Harry, R. Lee Ermey, Camille Cooper
games.hook: Can I follow the story while every other room demands a perfectly timed trap?
games.cheats: No codes confirmed for the Sega CD disc; FMV World has a full act-by-act trap walkthrough. The 25th Anniversary version includes a scene viewer.
games.video: Multi-camera filmed surveillance. The anniversary publisher advertises enhanced video; exact Sega CD frame rate and palette claims have not been measured for this brief.

games.trivia: Publisher listings credit Mary Lambert as director, Corey Haim, Debbie Harry and R. Lee Ermey among the cast, and Thomas Dolby for the score. No evidence here establishes the earlier best-selling-after-Night-Trap claim.

games.title: Prize Fighter
games.hook: A first-person boxing movie in noir black-and-white — the one Digital Pictures game that looks intentional.
games.cheats: Bonus video: in the Options menu press and hold A, B, C and Right, in that order, and keep holding until the sequence plays. (FMV World)
games.video: Full-screen black-and-white video, decent frame rate; the B&W choice hides compression well.
games.difficulty: Medium — rhythm-based; blocking windows are generous once learned.
games.endings: Win or lose each bout; title fight ending vs. loss cutscenes.
games.trivia: Director Ron Stein (fight choreographer on Rocky films). 2 discs because of the volume of branching fight footage.
games.notes: Black-and-white first-person boxing. 2-disc set.

games.title: Ground Zero Texas
games.cast: dir. Dwight H. Little (Halloween 4)
games.hook: Invasion of the Body Snatchers done as a Night Trap shooter, directed by the guy who made Halloween 4.
games.cheats: Level select: power on with Disc 2 in; at the 'Remove CD 2 Insert CD 1' message press A, B, Right, A, C, A, Down, A, B, Right, A (ABRACADABRA). Bonus video: lose on purpose and when the credits appear press C, B, A in a sweep, then Start. (FMV World)
games.video: Full-screen quadrants, ~10 fps per feed; noticeably grainy.
games.difficulty: Hard — managing four cameras while being shot at.
games.endings: Single ending with failure states per 'day'.
games.trivia: Budget reportedly over $3M, the largest of any Sega CD game. Sony Imagesoft marketed it heavily; 2021 'Nuclear Edition' remaster.
games.variants: Original 2-disc, PAL; Limited Run 2021 reprint and premium edition.
games.modern: Yes (Ground Zero Texas: Nuclear Edition — PS4, Switch, PC)
games.notes: Alien invasion shooter across four camera feeds. 2-disc set.

games.title: Corpse Killer
games.cast: Vincent Schiavelli
games.hook: Digital Pictures' zombie-island shooter with Vincent Schiavelli chewing scenery, in the version that also supports the Menacer.
games.cheats: Extra Datura bullets: when you're out of them and the Shadow Man or another strong enemy is attacking, hold A and tap B. Track 2 on an audio CD player plays a hidden message from Sewer Shark. No level select confirmed. (FMV World)
games.video: Full-screen, ~10-15 fps, very grainy jungle footage.
games.difficulty: Medium — zombies are slow; bosses are health-sponges.
games.endings: Single ending; game over if your 'infection' meter fills.
games.trivia: Shot in Puerto Rico. One of the last Digital Pictures games to get wide release; the 32X CD version adds colours.
games.variants: Sega CD, 32X CD, Limited Run 2019 reprints (both), 25th Anniversary Edition.
games.notes: Zombie shooter; also on 32X CD. Remastered on modern platforms by Limited Run (2019).

games.title: Supreme Warrior
games.cast: Hong Kong stunt team
games.hook: A Hong Kong kung-fu movie you fight your way through — the game that nearly works, which makes its failures funnier.
games.cheats: Difficulty settings only; no codes listed. Track 2 on an audio CD player has a backwards 'number 9' message. (GameFAQs)
games.video: Full-screen, 15 fps; the dubbed kung-fu footage is better shot than most.
games.difficulty: Hard — the blocking system is unforgiving, especially on real hardware input lag.
games.endings: Single ending; each disc covers two masters.
games.trivia: Produced in Hong Kong with local stunt teams; English dub recorded for the US release. Also on 3DO and 32X CD.
games.notes: Kung-fu FMV fighter; also on 32X CD. 2-disc set.

games.title: Slam City with Scottie Pippen
games.cast: Scottie Pippen
games.hook: Streetball FMV with Scottie Pippen in the year the Bulls were without Jordan — and it needs four discs to do it.
games.cheats: Super slams: press B, A, Left, Left before Fingers passes the ball. Bonus video: at the title press C for Options, then press and hold A, then B, then C until 'B15' appears top left; keep holding and press Up. (FMV World)
games.video: Full-screen, 15 fps, digitised player sprite over FMV court.
games.difficulty: Medium — mostly rhythm and reading the opponent's moves.
games.endings: Beat four opponents then Pippen; single ending.
games.trivia: Four discs, one per opponent; the most discs of any Sega CD game. Pippen appears only on disc 4.
games.variants: Sega CD 4-disc, 32X CD 4-disc. Incomplete sets are common — check for all four.
games.notes: Streetball with digitized player over FMV. 4-disc set; also on 32X CD.

games.title: Kids on Site
games.hook: The only children's FMV game on the system: you drive a bulldozer with a goofy foreman cheering you on.
games.video: Full-screen, decent frame rate; shot in daylight so it looks relatively clean.
games.trivia: Digital Pictures' attempt at an educational line; one of only a handful of Sega CD kids' titles.
games.modern: Yes (Windows and PS4 2022, PS5 2026; Screaming Villains and Limited Run)
games.notes: Children's game; drive construction equipment over FMV footage.

games.title: Make My Video: INXS
games.cast: INXS
games.cidTrigger: Full INXS tracks ('Heaven Sent', 'Not Enough Time', 'Baby Don't Cry')
games.hook: You are a music-video editor for INXS taking requests from a bored suburban family — three times, because Sega CD.
games.video: Full-screen, 64 colours; the music-video footage is the point and looks acceptable.
games.difficulty: None — assemble clips to match a client's request.
games.endings: Scored per video; no narrative ending.
games.trivia: The Make My Video series is frequently cited among the worst games ever; all four shipped within months of launch. Contains full tracks: 'Heaven Sent', 'Not Enough Time', 'Baby Don't Cry'.
games.notes: Cut together music videos from clip library. Three INXS songs.

games.title: Make My Video: Marky Mark and the Funky Bunch
games.cast: Marky Mark (Mark Wahlberg)
games.cidTrigger: Full tracks ('Good Vibrations', 'You Gotta Believe', 'I Need Money')
games.hook: Mark Wahlberg's rap career immortalised on Sega CD — the game AVGN and everyone else uses as shorthand for 'bad FMV'.
games.video: Full-screen music videos; clip library includes stock footage.
games.trivia: Tracks: 'Good Vibrations', 'You Gotta Believe', 'I Need Money'. The 'client' framing (callers phoning in requests) is shared across the series.
games.notes: Same engine as other Make My Video titles.

games.title: Make My Video: Kris Kross
games.cast: Kris Kross
games.cidTrigger: Full tracks ('Jump', 'Warm It Up', 'I Missed the Bus')
games.hook: 'Jump' as a game, from the era when Sony thought kids wanted to edit music videos on a console.
games.video: Full-screen music videos.
games.trivia: Tracks: 'Jump', 'Warm It Up', 'I Missed the Bus'. Cheapest of the four today.
games.notes: Same engine as other Make My Video titles.

games.title: Power Factory Featuring C+C Music Factory
games.alt: Make My Video: C+C Music Factory
games.cast: C+C Music Factory
games.cidTrigger: Full tracks ('Gonna Make You Sweat', 'Here We Go', 'Things That Make You Go Hmmm')
games.hook: The fourth Make My Video game, renamed because 'C+C Music Factory: Make My Video' apparently wasn't catchy enough.
games.video: Full-screen music videos.
games.trivia: Tracks: 'Gonna Make You Sweat (Everybody Dance Now)', 'Here We Go', 'Things That Make You Go Hmmm...'.
games.notes: Fourth Make My Video title, released under a different name.

games.title: Mad Dog McCree
games.hook: The arcade's first live-action light-gun game, with the Menacer-or-mouse question built right into the episode.
games.cheats: Options: difficulty and lives; stage order is partly selectable in-game (bank, saloon, etc.).
games.video: Full-screen, ~10 fps, 64-colour laserdisc footage looks rough but readable.
games.difficulty: Medium — short reaction windows; much easier with a mouse than a controller.
games.endings: Single ending; game over screens are the undertaker/prospector gags.
games.trivia: ALG's 1990 arcade original was the first laserdisc game in years to be a hit; the Sega CD port was ALG's first console release.
games.variants: US only (ALG). Compatible with Menacer, Justifier, Sega Mouse.
games.modern: No verified current digital sale; original discs and legacy Digital Leisure editions (platforms vary).
games.notes: Supports Sega Menacer or controller. Arcade original 1990.

games.title: Mad Dog II: The Lost Gold
games.hook: The sequel with a choose-your-guide structure, and the rarest and priciest of the four ALG discs.
games.cheats: Cheat mode: at the menu screen, before touching anything else, press B, B, A+B, A+B+C, A+C (a sound confirms). Then shoot the map within a second when the arrow-riddled man hands it over, and shoot the Padre's half as it rotates, to enable unlimited ammo, unlimited lives, C to auto-shoot and a Gatling gun mode. (FMV World)
games.video: Same as Mad Dog McCree.
games.endings: Three guides give three different routes to the same ending.
games.trivia: Arcade 1992. Sega CD release was late (1994) and small, hence today's price.
games.modern: No verified current digital sale; original discs and legacy Digital Leisure editions (platforms vary).
games.notes: Sequel; Menacer or controller.

games.title: Crime Patrol
games.hook: ALG's modern-day cop shooter where you climb from beat cop to anti-terrorist unit in 30 minutes of 1993 stock-action footage.
games.cheats: Difficulty and lives; rank progression (Rookie → Delta Force) is fixed.
games.video: Same engine; the urban footage is murkier than the westerns.
games.difficulty: Hard — fast draws, lots of innocents to avoid.
games.endings: Single ending after Delta Force stage.
games.trivia: Arcade 1993. The Sega CD port is one of the more expensive discs; the DVD-player version was a 2000s curiosity.
games.modern: No verified current digital sale; original discs and legacy Digital Leisure editions (platforms vary).
games.notes: Menacer or controller.

games.title: Who Shot Johnny Rock?
games.hook: A light-gun murder mystery with a randomised killer — the only ALG game that's actually replayable.
games.cheats: Difficulty settings; you can revisit locations freely to gather clues.
games.video: Same engine; 1930s costume footage is well lit.
games.difficulty: Medium — shooting is easy, the whodunnit requires the right clue order.
games.endings: Culprit is randomised each game (5 suspects), so several endings.
games.trivia: Arcade 1991. Features a 'budget' system: pay for your lives with cash earned from clues.
games.modern: No verified current digital sale; original discs and legacy Digital Leisure editions (platforms vary).
games.notes: 1930s gangster detective theme. Menacer or controller.

games.title: Tomcat Alley
games.developer: Sega Multimedia Studio / The Code Monkeys
games.alsoOn: Windows retail port (1995 Sega PC lineup); current digital purchase and modern runtime not verified here.
games.hook: Can I win an aerial action movie from the back seat using a cursor?
games.video: Filmed flight action with an interactive HUD. No measured frame-rate claim; test reticle, HUD edges and dialogue in the saved recording.
games.difficulty: Medium — mostly timed clicks; later missions punish slow target acquisition.
games.endings: Single ending; failure sequences per mission.
games.trivia: The manual credits Sam Nicholson as director, John Zuur Platten as writer, Clay Lacy for aerial photography and The Code Monkeys for programming. These credits do not establish the earlier US Navy footage-licensing claim.
games.variants: Sega CD for Season Zero. A Windows retail port exists; NintendoComplete's PC playthrough describes improved graphics and mouse input. That is an attributed comparison, not a tested route on a current PC. No new console is needed for the main episode.

Proposed personal speed-clear: new game to credits, default difficulty, real time, with retry policy stated. Optional PC comparison: one briefing and combat sequence. games.title: Surgical Strike
games.hook: Sega's hovercraft commando shooter, and the only Sega CD game whose 32X version was released exclusively in Brazil.
games.cheats: No codes listed on GameFAQs. Tip: at the end of stage one, shoot the machine in the bottom-right corner with the Gatling gun to stop the missile launches. (GameFAQs)
games.video: Full-screen, ~15 fps; the 32X CD version has far better colour.
games.difficulty: Medium-hard — route choices with instant failure branches.
games.trivia: Code Monkeys developed; Tec Toy published the 32X CD version in Brazil in 1995. Live actors plus miniatures.
games.variants: Sega CD (US, PAL), 32X CD (Brazil only, very expensive).
games.notes: Hovercraft shooter. The 32X CD version was released only in Brazil (Tec Toy).

games.title: Midnight Raiders
games.hook: The Apache-helicopter cousin of Tomcat Alley that nobody remembers, from the same Sega studio.
games.video: Full-screen helicopter footage, ~15 fps.
games.trivia: Stargate Productions handled the shoot; Sega Multimedia Studio's last rail shooter before Wirehead.
games.notes: Apache helicopter shooter with a long FMV campaign.

games.title: Wirehead
games.hook: Can I guide an ordinary dad through an action movie when the controller literally controls his body?
games.cheats: Shortcut: on the first level ride the skateboard off the loading dock and press Up twice to land in the jeep and go straight to the airport. No level select confirmed. (FMV World)
games.video: Filmed action with directional prompts. Exact video window dimensions and frame rate have not been measured for this brief.
games.endings: Single ending; many comedic death scenes.
games.trivia: The original manual credits James Riley as writer/director and Steve Witting as Wirehead. Its Multiple Paths section confirms that some situations allow more than one escape route.
games.variants: Use the Sega CD release and compare alternate routes on the same disc. A contemporary schedule advertised a 32X-CD edition, but that is not evidence it shipped. No released second edition verified in this pass.
games.notes: Season Zero episode proposal: establish Ned's remote-control premise, compare a safe route with a shortcut, then build to the timed attempt. Sega-16 describes battery-based retries and converging chapter routes; verify rollback behavior on this disc. Capture a good choice, wrong choice and battery loss. Recheck current board rules before a submission. Sources: https://r.mprd.se/Sega%20CD/Manuals/Wirehead%20%28U%29.pdf https://www.sega-16.com/2008/09/wirehead/
games.wherePlay: Season Zero route: original Sega CD on the owned tower, through the owned RetroTINK and HDMI capture card. Capture NOT TESTED: no recordings yet (Tom, 2026-10-25). Models, cables, audio routing and recording settings remain to be logged. Use the short and sustained capture checks in docs/season-zero-briefs.md before a full attempt.

games.title: Fahrenheit
games.hook: Firefighter FMV where the box contains both Sega CD and 32X CD discs, so you can show the same footage on both in one episode.
games.cheats: Level select code exists for the Sega CD disc (verify).
games.video: Full-screen on 32X CD with true colour; Sega CD disc is 64-colour and much grainier — a built-in comparison.
games.trivia: Sega's last FMV production; the 32X CD version is considered the definitive one. Sold only as the dual-disc bundle in the US.
games.variants: US dual-disc only. Confirm both discs are present when buying.
games.notes: Sold as a 2-disc set containing both the Sega CD and 32X CD versions. First-person firefighter exploration.

games.title: Mighty Morphin Power Rangers
games.alsoOn: Sega CD only (Genesis/SNES games are different)
games.cast: Original MMPR TV cast
games.cidTrigger: TV series footage & theme
games.hook: Power Rangers as a QTE fighting game built from actual Season 1 episodes — different from every other MMPR game of the era.
games.cheats: Level skip: at the Difficulty/Start screen press B, A, C, C, A, B, A (a tone confirms); press Start during play to skip the level. Hidden video: at the title press A, B, B, A, C, A, B, B. (FMV World)
games.video: Full-screen TV footage, ~10 fps; colours suffer badly from the 64-colour limit.
games.trivia: Built on the same engine Sega reused for Kamen Rider ZO in Japan. Uses episodes including the Green Ranger arc.
games.notes: Uses actual TV show footage; fights are timed button presses over video. Some sprite-based elements.

games.title: The Masked Rider: Kamen Rider ZO
games.cast: Kou Domon
games.cidTrigger: Film footage
games.hook: The 1993 Kamen Rider ZO movie chopped into a Sega CD fighting game, which Sega then rebuilt as Power Rangers for the US.
games.video: Full-screen film footage, ~10 fps.
games.trivia: Toei Video published; the engine was later used for the US Power Rangers game. The film is 48 minutes long, so the game covers most of it.
games.variants: JP only. PriceCharting lists it as 'Masked Rider' under US Sega CD.
games.notes: Japan only. Built on the Power Rangers engine using the 1993 Kamen Rider ZO film footage.

games.title: Road Rash
games.cidTrigger: Licensed soundtrack (Soundgarden, Monster Magnet, Paw, Swervedriver, Therapy?, Hammerbox)
games.hook: The best Road Rash with the grunge soundtrack and live-action cop-arrest cutscenes — the FMV is garnish, but it's good garnish.
games.cheats: Password system; cheat passwords for cash and bikes exist (verify).
games.video: Cutscenes are full-screen, ~15 fps; gameplay is standard sprites.
games.trivia: Shares its FMV and soundtrack with the 3DO/Saturn/PS1 versions. Soundtrack: Soundgarden, Paw, Hammerbox, Monster Magnet, Swervedriver, Therapy?.
games.notes: Standard Road Rash with live-action FMV cutscenes between races. Gameplay is not FMV.

games.title: Loadstar: The Legend of Tully Bodine
games.cast: Ned Beatty, Barry Primus
games.hook: Ned Beatty in a sci-fi truck movie from Rocket Science Games, the $100M startup that produced three games and vanished.
games.cheats: No level select listed. Hidden Mort-Pong minigame: when Mort appears, pause and press C, A, Left, Left, A, C, A, Left, Left, A. (GameFAQs)
games.video: Full-screen pre-rendered CG with composited actors, ~15 fps.
games.difficulty: Hard — lots of trial-and-error truck steering.
games.trivia: Rocket Science Games raised enormous VC money in 1993-95 and collapsed by 1997; Loadstar and Cadillacs & Dinosaurs were its Sega CD output.
games.notes: CG truck-driving shooter with live-action actors composited in. Ned Beatty and Barry Primus star.

games.title: Novastorm
games.hook: Psygnosis's Rebel Assault-style shooter that's actually hard, with one of the pricier discs on the system.
games.video: Full-screen pre-rendered CG, ~15 fps, reduced from the PC original's colour depth.
games.trivia: Sega CD version is a substantially different game from PC/PS1 ('Scavenger 4' in Japan). Novastorm's CG was state-of-the-art in 1994.
games.notes: Spaceship sprite over streamed CG backgrounds. Sega CD version differs substantially from PC/PS1.

games.title: Microcosm
games.hook: Does a controllable ship over a prerecorded human body make the cinematic future fun to play?
games.cheats: Level passwords (icons: A ring with 6 spheres, B sphere with 2 rings, C sphere with ring and 4 spheres, D sphere with 4 orbiting spheres, E sphere with 6 spheres): Level 2 B D E A, Level 3 E E D B, Level 4 B A D E. Pressing eject freezes enemies so you can shoot them. (GameFAQs)
games.video: Movable ship over prerecorded CG tunnel backgrounds, described in Sega-16's review. Exact Sega CD frame rate and dimensions are not measured; inspect ship visibility and dark-scene detail in capture.
games.difficulty: Hard — the Sega CD port is sluggish.
games.trivia: Credited development interviews describe FM Towns development, Fujitsu's involvement and compression compromises. Mike Clarke recalls different music licensing and music work for later versions; DOS soundtrack details still need edition-specific checking.
games.variants: Use Sega CD for Season Zero. Contemporary CD32 coverage reports substantial rewriting and a visible ship replacing the FM Towns crosshair. DOS soundtrack descriptions conflict; the prior DOS best-version pick remains provisional. CD-i promotional footage is not proof of a complete publicly playable prototype.
games.notes: Season Zero episode proposal: distinguish the controllable ship from the prerecorded tunnel, explain one sourced compression compromise, then compare the spectacular intro with enemy visibility in play. Proposed personal speed-clear: power-on to credits, default difficulty, real time; keep separate from new-game-start runs. Do not repeat unverified CD32 launch-title, Sega-team conversion or 12 fps claims. Sources: https://www.timeextension.com/features/the-making-of-microcosm-cd-rom-gamings-first-aaa-title https://www.amigareviews.leveluphost.com/microcos.htm https://www.sega-16.com/2010/10/microcosm/
games.wherePlay: Season Zero route: original Sega CD on the owned tower, through the owned RetroTINK and HDMI capture card. Capture NOT TESTED: no recordings yet (Tom, 2026-10-25). Models, cables, audio routing and recording settings remain to be logged. Use the short and sustained capture checks in docs/season-zero-briefs.md before a full attempt. Optional CD32/FM Towns comparison; DOS configuration and all secondary captures remain untested.

games.title: Star Wars: Rebel Assault
games.cast: Film clips
games.cidTrigger: Star Wars film clips & John Williams score
games.hook: The game that sold CD-ROM drives in 1993, in the console port where the Death Star trench is 64 colours.
games.cheats: Password system; passwords to skip to any chapter are well documented.
games.video: Full-screen pre-rendered CG plus film clips, ~15 fps; 64 colours hurt the space scenes.
games.trivia: LucasArts' first CD-only game; the Sega CD port was done in-house. Limited Run reprinted it in 2023 with a premium edition.
games.variants: US (JVC), PAL, JP (Victor); Limited Run reprint and premium edition.
games.modern: Yes (Limited Run reprint; original PC version on GOG)
games.notes: Streamed CG with sprite overlay plus clips from the films. Very common.

games.title: A/X-101
games.hook: Micronet's Rebel Assault knockoff with a giant mech instead of an X-wing — cheap, common, and more fun than its reputation.
games.cheats: Expanded options: at the title highlight Options and press Left, Left, Left, Right, Right, Right, Up, Down, Up, Down, A, B, C, Start to add a sound test, collision toggle, cutscene viewer and level select. (GameFAQs)
games.video: Full-screen pre-rendered CG, ~12 fps.
games.trivia: Micronet also made Heavy Nova; A/X-101 was published in the US by Absolute Entertainment (Penn & Teller's publisher).
games.notes: Rebel Assault-style mech shooter. Cheap and common in NA.

games.title: Silpheed
games.source: 1986 PC-88 shooter; Sega CD version is a reimagining
games.hook: The shooter that faked 3D polygon space battles by streaming them off the disc — and it still looks good.
games.cheats: Stage select: during the intro press Down, Down, Up, Up, Right, Left, Right, Left, A, B, Start, then pick the stage and press A. Debug mode: controller 2 at the opening, Left, A, B, Up, Down, Up, Up, Left, Right, C, Right, Down, B. 10 continues on your last continue: during the intro movie Right, Up, A, B, C, Left, Left, Down, C, A, Start. (GameFAQs)
games.video: Full-screen streamed backgrounds, 15 fps, polygon ship on top.
games.difficulty: Medium-hard — 12 stages, no continues on higher settings.
games.trivia: Game Arts' showcase for the Sega CD; the 'backgrounds are FMV' trick was widely misunderstood at the time as real-time 3D.
games.notes: Polygon ship over streamed pre-rendered backgrounds. Plays as a real shooter; FMV is the backdrop.

games.title: Iron Helix
games.hook: A CG Myst-meets-Alien where you pilot a probe through a derelict ship while a robot hunts you — the scariest Sega CD game.
games.video: Pre-rendered CG movement clips, small window, ~10 fps.
games.difficulty: Hard — the Defender robot hunts you; one mistake is death.
games.endings: Single ending; game over if the ship reaches the planet.
games.trivia: Drew Pictures' Mac CD-ROM original (1993); Spectrum HoloByte ported it. 2 discs.
games.notes: Explore a derelict ship via a probe; movement is pre-rendered video clips. 2-disc set.

games.title: Mansion of Hidden Souls
games.alt: Yumemi Yakata: Tobira no Oku ni Dareka ga... (JP)
games.alsoOn: Saturn sequel ('The Mansion of Hidden Souls', 1996)
games.hook: A Japanese Myst about a mansion full of butterflies that used to be people, made before Myst existed.
games.video: Pre-rendered CG transitions, small window; soft and dreamy, suits the game.
games.trivia: System Sacom's 'Yumemi Yakata' (1993) predates Myst's console ports; a Saturn sequel followed in 1996.
games.notes: Myst-like point-and-click where every move is a streamed CG clip. JP 1993, NA/EU 1994. Saturn sequel exists.

games.title: Sherlock Holmes: Consulting Detective Vol. I
games.alsoOn: Original DOS/Mac and other CD-ROM ports; Zojoi restored the three Volume I cases as separate modern games. The Steam Collection is those three cases, not Volumes I–III.
games.cast: Peter Farley (Holmes)
games.hook: Can I solve a filmed mystery efficiently without turning deduction into a memorized answer sheet?
games.video: Filmed testimony in the original Sega CD presentation. Compare a matching interview with Zojoi's restoration; exact Sega CD dimensions, frame rate and content parity remain unmeasured.
games.difficulty: Medium — real deduction required; scoring compares your path to Holmes's.
games.endings: Each case ends with a trial; score depends on route.
games.trivia: Original ICOM art director and Zojoi cofounder David Marsh told Joe Pranevich that recovered Beta SP source tapes were redigitized for the restoration.
games.variants: Volume I: The Mummy's Curse, The Mystified Murderess and The Tin Soldier. For a modern comparison buy one restored case, or the three-case Steam Collection for all of Volume I. The restoration comparison reports redesigned research screens, subtitles, hints and a discovery log; confirm details in the installed version.
games.notes: Season Zero episode proposal: follow a newspaper lead into an interview and courtroom answer, then contrast deduction with a practiced route. Match the same testimony and research screen in the restoration. Proposed personal speed-clear: one named case, case selection to verdict, real time, declaring hints and prior knowledge. This is not an official-record claim. Sources: https://store.steampowered.com/app/374010/ https://advgamer.blogspot.com/2016/09/consulting-detective-alternate-versions.html?m=0 https://advgamer.blogspot.com/2016/09/a-conversation-with-david-marsh.html
games.wherePlay: Season Zero route: original Sega CD on the owned tower, through the owned RetroTINK and HDMI capture card. Capture NOT TESTED: no recordings yet (Tom, 2026-10-25). Models, cables, audio routing and recording settings remain to be logged. Use the short and sustained capture checks in docs/season-zero-briefs.md before a full attempt. Optional comparison: Zojoi's Mummy's Curse on Steam, separately from the original DOS edition.

games.title: Sherlock Holmes: Consulting Detective Vol. II
games.cast: Peter Farley (Holmes)
games.hook: Three more cases, including 'The Tin Soldier', generally considered the best case in the series.
games.video: Same engine.
games.trivia: Cases: The Two Lions, The Pilfered Paintings, The Murdered Munitions Magnate.
games.modern: No (this volume); no restored edition verified. The later restoration covers a different volume.
games.notes: Three more cases, same engine.
games.wherePlay: Original disc on the appropriate system or a compatible emulator; no restoration of this volume verified.

games.title: Sherlock Holmes: Consulting Detective Vol. III
games.cast: Peter Farley (Holmes)
games.hook: The volume America never got on Sega CD — English video, Japanese menus.
games.video: Same engine.
games.trivia: Cases: The Solicitous Solicitor, The Banker's Final Debt, The Thames Murders. Victor published in Japan only.
games.modern: No (this volume); no restored edition verified. The later restoration covers a different volume.
games.notes: Japan only on Mega CD. English video with Japanese text/menus. PRICE: No PriceCharting listing; check eBay sold / Yahoo Japan Auctions.
games.wherePlay: Original disc on the appropriate system or a compatible emulator; no restoration of this volume verified.

games.title: Dracula Unleashed
games.hook: A sequel to the Dracula novel, played as a timetable puzzle through Victorian London, with a gloriously hammy cast.
games.cheats: None; time management is the puzzle.
games.video: Small-to-medium window, ~10 fps; lots of darkly lit footage that compresses poorly.
games.difficulty: Hard — a strict timetable; being in the wrong place at the wrong time kills you.
games.endings: Single success ending; many death endings.
games.trivia: ICOM's follow-up to Sherlock Holmes; shot in Chicago. The 3DO version is clearer; the Sega CD version came first.
games.notes: Sequel-in-spirit to Stoker's novel; travel London, trigger video scenes. 2-disc set.

games.title: The Lawnmower Man
games.alsoOn: PC/Mac CD, 3DO (CD versions share FMV); SNES/Genesis carts differ
games.cast: Jeff Fahey, Pierce Brosnan (clips)
games.cidTrigger: 1992 film footage
games.hook: A game about a movie about VR, played on a console that could barely show video — and it's one of the most expensive discs now.
games.video: FMV/CG stages are full-screen ~12 fps; platform stages are sprites.
games.difficulty: Hard — platform stages are cheap, cyberspace stages are trial and error.
games.trivia: Sales Curve's CD build shares its FMV with the PC/3DO versions; the SNES/Genesis carts are a different game. Pierce Brosnan appears in clips.
games.notes: Mix of side-scrolling platform stages and FMV/CG 'cyberspace' sequences using film footage.
games.criticSrc: average of 2 reviews on Wikipedia (MF, MMS)

games.title: Dune
games.cast: Kyle MacLachlan, Sting (clips)
games.cidTrigger: Lynch film clips, Toto score
games.hook: Cryo's Dune with David Lynch's movie cut into it — the only way to play the 1992 game with Kyle MacLachlan talking to you.
games.video: Film clips in a small window, ~10 fps; in-game art is hand-drawn.
games.difficulty: Medium — a slow strategy game; losing is hard once you learn spice management.
games.endings: Single ending; game over if Harkonnens take Arrakis.
games.trivia: Virgin added the film clips for the CD versions; the Sega CD version also adds a CD soundtrack (Stéphane Picq's 'Spice Opera' partly).
games.modern: Yes (PC version on GOG, without film clips in some releases)
games.notes: Sega CD version adds extensive clips from the 1984 Lynch film to the PC adventure game.

games.title: Wheel of Fortune
games.alsoOn: Sega CD version is unique; cart versions have no FMV
games.cast: Vanna White
games.cidTrigger: Show theme & footage
games.hook: Vanna White on Sega CD, turning letters in 64 colours.
games.video: Vanna clips in a window, ~10 fps; board is standard graphics.
games.trivia: Sony Imagesoft's game-show line (with Jeopardy!) added FMV only on Sega CD.
games.notes: FMV Vanna White; puzzle board is standard graphics.

games.title: Jeopardy!
games.alsoOn: Sega CD version is unique; cart versions have no FMV
games.cast: Alex Trebek
games.cidTrigger: Show theme & footage
games.hook: Alex Trebek on Sega CD — the cheapest FMV game on the system and still playable as a trivia night.
games.video: Trebek clips in a small window; less video than Wheel.
games.trivia: Question database is early-90s era; expect dated categories.
games.notes: FMV Alex Trebek intros and reactions; less video than Wheel.

games.title: Trivial Pursuit
games.cidTrigger: Video clip questions
games.hook: Trivial Pursuit with video questions, from the brief period when every board game got a 'multimedia' edition.
games.video: Short video clips as questions; small window.
games.trivia: Western Technologies developed; one of the last third-party Sega CD releases in 1995.
games.notes: Some questions use video clips. Publisher attribution uncertain; verify on the box.

games.title: NFL's Greatest Teams
games.cast: NFL Films narration
games.cidTrigger: NFL Films footage & music
games.hook: Sega's football game built around NFL Films footage — the 'greatest teams' are the 60s-80s dynasties.
games.video: NFL Films clips in a window between plays and in the intro.
games.trivia: Reuses the Joe Montana Sports Talk Football engine; one of the few sports games with real NFL Films licensing.
games.notes: Joe Montana engine with NFL Films footage and FMV commentary.

games.title: ESPN Baseball Tonight
games.cast: Chris Berman
games.cidTrigger: ESPN branding, Chris Berman segments
games.hook: Chris Berman introducing a baseball game that's otherwise the Genesis cart.
games.video: Chris Berman intro/segments in a window.
games.trivia: Park Place Productions developed the whole ESPN line for Sony Imagesoft.
games.notes: FMV Chris Berman segments; gameplay is standard.

games.title: ESPN National Hockey Night
games.cidTrigger: ESPN branding & commentary
games.hook: The ESPN hockey game, notable mostly for being the cheapest way to see ESPN-branded FMV on Sega CD.
games.video: ESPN-styled video segments in a window.
games.trivia: Same line as Baseball Tonight.
games.notes: FMV commentary; gameplay is standard.

games.title: ESPN NBA Hangtime '95
games.cidTrigger: ESPN branding & commentary
games.hook: A middling basketball game that now costs more than Night Trap because almost nobody bought it.
games.video: Video segments in a window.
games.trivia: One of the rarest licensed Sega CD releases (1995); its price is a scarcity story, not a quality one.
games.notes: FMV commentary; gameplay is standard.

games.title: ESPN Sunday Night NFL
games.cast: Chris Berman
games.cidTrigger: ESPN branding, Chris Berman segments
games.hook: Chris Berman again, this time for football.
games.video: Berman segments in a window.
games.trivia: Ringler Studios developed; Sega CD version adds the video over the cart version.
games.notes: FMV Chris Berman segments; gameplay is standard.

games.title: Heavenly Symphony: Formula One World Championship 1993
games.cast: 1993 F1 drivers (footage)
games.cidTrigger: Real F1 race footage (FOM)
games.hook: A Japanese F1 game with real 1993 race footage — Senna's last full season — that costs five dollars.
games.video: Real F1 footage between races, small window; gameplay is sprite-based.
games.difficulty: Medium-hard — a serious racing sim for its time.
games.trivia: Sega's own F1 licence (Japan). The '93 footage includes Senna, Prost and Schumacher. Mega CD only.
games.notes: Japan only. Real 1993 F1 season footage between races.

games.title: Jurassic Park
games.cidTrigger: Film license, Williams score cues
games.hook: Sega's own Jurassic Park is a point-and-click adventure, not the platformer, and it opens with the dinosaurs in 64-colour video.
games.cheats: Debug 'Node Jumper': pick up the rock at the start, select it, move the cursor to the green strip between mountain and sea (a little left) and press C until it beeps; then hold Start on controller 2 to jump to any level or watch any video, and C on controller 2 gives that area's items. (GameFAQs)
games.video: Short FMV clips and a CG intro in a window; the in-game adventure is first-person stills.
games.endings: Single ending; game over when the clock expires or you're eaten.
games.trivia: Sega Multimedia Studio developed; entirely separate from the Genesis/SNES games. Features a 'dinosaur identification' video database.
games.notes: Point-and-click adventure with short FMV intro/cutscenes and Richard Attenborough-style briefing videos.

games.title: Bram Stoker's Dracula
games.cast: Gary Oldman, Keanu Reeves (clips)
games.cidTrigger: Film clips, Kilar score
games.hook: Coppola's Dracula as a bad platformer, with Gary Oldman clips as the reward for finishing each stage.
games.cheats: Cheat mode: when 'Beware' appears press A, Left, Up, C, A, Right, Down. Then hold buttons and press Start to pick a level (B+C = level 3, A = 4, A+C = 5, A+B = 6). An infinite-lives combo also unlocks. (GameFAQs)
games.video: Film clips in a window between levels, ~10 fps.
games.trivia: Psygnosis developed all versions; Sony Imagesoft's CD version added the clips and a CD soundtrack.
games.variants: US, PAL; US 'Mary Shelley's Frankenstein & Bram Stoker's Dracula' 2-pack.
games.notes: Platformer with clips from the 1992 Coppola film between stages.

games.title: Cliffhanger
games.alsoOn: Genesis, SNES, NES, Game Boy (no FMV)
games.cast: Sylvester Stallone (clips)
games.cidTrigger: Film clips
games.hook: Stallone's mountain movie as a beat-'em-up, with the movie's best scenes played at 10 fps.
games.cheats: Level skip: at the title, on controller 2, press Start, C, B, A, Right, Left, Right, Left ('Level Skip' appears); pause and press C to skip. Controller 2 at the title: A, B, C, Down, Up = snowboarding sequences only. (GameFAQs)
games.video: Film clips in a window between levels.
games.trivia: Malibu Interactive (the comics company's game arm) developed; one of the lowest-rated Sega CD games.
games.notes: Film clips between stages. Verify clip count; a modest amount of video.

games.title: The Amazing Spider-Man vs. The Kingpin
games.alsoOn: Genesis, Game Gear, Master System (no FMV)
games.cast: Voice cast
games.hook: The Genesis Spider-Man expanded with animated cutscenes, new levels and a vocal theme — the rare CD upgrade that's better.
games.cheats: Level passwords: 2 ELECTRO, 3 WALLABY, 4 GALLON66, 5 FALCON499, 6 HELPINHAND, 7 PUBLIC45, 8 KIDNEY2, 9 PENCIL6. Unlimited web: set Easy with A = punch, B = jump, C = web. Three endings depend on saving Mary Jane in the Kingpin fight. (GameFAQs)
games.video: Animated cutscenes in a window with voice acting.
games.difficulty: Medium-hard — expanded from the Genesis game with new levels.
games.endings: Single ending; bomb timer failure ending.
games.trivia: Technopop's CD edition adds Vulture and Mysterio levels, a save system and a vocal theme song.
games.notes: Animated video cutscenes with voice acting added for the CD version.

games.title: Sonic the Hedgehog CD
games.cidTrigger: Toei intro/ending animation, 'Sonic Boom' / JP vocal themes
games.hook: The best-selling Sega CD game, with an opening cartoon that is still the console's signature video moment.
games.cheats: Sound-test codes unlock the 'secret' screens (incl. the infamous 'Fun is infinite' screen) — well documented.
games.video: Full-screen animated intro/ending at ~15 fps; the only clean-looking video on the system because it's animation designed for it.
games.endings: Good and bad endings (collect all Time Stones).
games.trivia: Intro/ending animated by Toei (Studio Junio); the US release swapped the JP vocal songs for Spencer Nilsen's score and 'Sonic Boom'.
games.variants: US, PAL, JP; US Not-For-Resale pack-in version.
games.modern: Yes (Sonic CD 2011 remaster on everything; Sonic Origins)
games.notes: Animated intro and ending movies by Toei/Studio Junio. JP Sept, EU Oct, NA Nov 1993.

games.title: Mortal Kombat
games.cidTrigger: 'Mortal Monday' TV spot
games.hook: The Genesis Mortal Kombat with CD audio and the 'Mortal Monday' TV ad as its intro — a 30-second episode's worth of FMV.
games.cheats: Blood code and standard MK1 codes apply; cheat menu code exists (verify).
games.video: The 'Mortal Monday' commercial plays as a full-screen intro.
games.trivia: Arena/Acclaim's CD version is otherwise identical to the cart; loading times were widely mocked.
games.notes: Includes the 'Mortal Monday' TV commercial as an FMV intro; otherwise the Genesis game with CD audio.

games.title: WWF Rage in the Cage
games.cast: 20 WWF wrestlers (Bret Hart, Undertaker, etc.)
games.cidTrigger: WWF/WWE footage & entrance music
games.hook: Twenty 1993 WWF wrestlers with their real entrance videos, in the Royal Rumble engine, with a cage.
games.video: Wrestler entrance/profile videos in a window.
games.trivia: Roster includes Bret Hart, Undertaker, Yokozuna, Razor Ramon; the only WWF game on Sega CD.
games.notes: Short FMV entrance/profile videos for each wrestler.

games.title: Citizen X
games.hook: A Digital Pictures game that was finished in 1993, shelved, and sold in 2002 by a fan publisher — with a 15-minute time limit.
games.cheats: Unknown; the released beta has no documented codes.
games.video: FMV cut-ins in a window; the platform game is sprites.
games.difficulty: Hard — a 15-minute real-time limit for the whole game.
games.trivia: Good Deal Games released the near-final beta with Digital Pictures' blessing; it's unlicensed by Sega. Hasbro co-produced.
games.variants: Good Deal Games 2002 release only (jewel case, no official Sega branding).
games.notes: Built 1993, cancelled, then sold commercially by Good Deal Games in 2002 as a near-complete beta. Side-scroller with FMV cut-ins. Pricey on the secondary market. PRICE: PriceCharting lists it but has no recorded sales; recent eBay asks $150-300 CIB.

games.title: Bug Blasters: The Exterminators
games.publisher: Good Deal Games (2001 release; planned Sony Imagesoft)
games.hook: Ghostbusters-with-bugs, shelved in 1995, released in 2001, and the star of AGDQ 2026's Awful Block.
games.video: Full-screen, ~10 fps; even by Sega CD standards the video is murky.
games.difficulty: Very hard — many players report it is barely finishable on real hardware.
games.trivia: Sony Imagesoft was to publish it as 'The Exterminators'; Good Deal Games renamed it. Shown at Summer CES 1994.
games.notes: Completed 1995, shelved, then sold by Good Deal Games in 2001. Ghostbusters-style bug exterminators. Typically $150-250 CIB.

games.title: Penn & Teller's Smoke and Mirrors
games.cast: Penn Jillette, Teller
games.hook: Home of Desert Bus — the game designed to annoy Janet Reno — leaked 15 years after its publisher went bankrupt.
games.cheats: None; some minigames are deliberately unwinnable (that's the joke).
games.video: Full-screen FMV in the 'cheat' games; Desert Bus is a standard driving screen.
games.difficulty: Varies; Desert Bus is 8 real-time hours per point.
games.trivia: Absolute Entertainment folded in 1995 before release; a near-final disc leaked in 2010 via Frank Cifaldi. Lou Reed cameos in some segments (verify).
games.variants: Prototype image only (Sega CD; 3DO/PC versions never finished).
games.modern: No (Desert Bus has fan remakes; a VR version exists)
games.notes: Never sold. Near-final prototype leaked online in 2010 and is freely downloadable; playable via emulator or burned disc. Home of 'Desert Bus'. Several FMV-driven minigames with Penn & Teller. PRICE: Never sold; prototype download only.

games.title: Maximum Surge
games.alsoOn: Footage recut into the 2003 film 'Game Over'
games.cast: Yasmine Bleeth, Walter Koenig
games.hook: The FMV game that was never released and became a direct-to-video movie instead.
games.video: N/A
games.trivia: Shot 1995 with Yasmine Bleeth and Walter Koenig; after Digital Pictures folded the footage was edited into 'Game Over' (2003).
games.notes: Shot with Yasmine Bleeth and Walter Koenig; never released and no disc dump has surfaced. Footage was recut into the 2003 movie 'Game Over'. Listed for completeness only. PRICE: Not obtainable.

games.title: MegaRace
games.cast: Christian Erickson as host Lance Boyle
games.hook: A racing game whose tracks are streamed pre-rendered video, hosted by the smarmiest game-show host of the decade, Lance Boyle.
games.video: Full-screen streamed CG track, ~15 fps, 64 colours on Sega CD; cars are sprites over the video.
games.difficulty: Medium — the car can't leave the pre-rendered road, so it's about weapons timing.
games.endings: Single ending after all tracks; Lance Boyle reacts to results.
games.trivia: Cryo's showcase for CD-ROM; the Sega CD port was published by Mindscape. Lance Boyle's segments were shot against greenscreen and inserted between races.
games.notes: Added after the first pass: same streamed-background tech as Silpheed and Novastorm. Sega CD 'MegaRace' PriceCharting: $22.50 loose / $48.67 CIB / $71.70 new.

games.title: Mad Dog McCree
games.publisher: American Laser Games (NA/EU); not released in Japan
games.alsoOn: Arcade, Sega CD, CD-i, DOS/Windows, DVD TV game, Wii, iOS, 3DS, PS3
games.cast: Ben Zeller (Prospector), Russ/Rusty Dillen (Mad Dog), Lori Dillen (barfly), Carol Eason (undertaker)
games.hook: The game that started the live-action light-gun craze, shot in New Mexico for $125k with local actors and a stunt-caliber spittoon count.
games.video: Reduced window (not full screen), Cinepak-style compression ~15 fps; Edge called it 'tolerable', GamePro poor — verify exact size
games.difficulty: Easy once memorized; pad cursor is very slow, nearly requires the Gamegun
games.endings: Linear; one ending (defeat Mad Dog in the final showdown); branching only via mistakes/deaths
games.trivia: Budget was about $125,000; Russ Dillen dyed his blonde hair black to play Mad Dog. The 3DO port shipped before the Gamegun, so early buyers had to aim with the control pad.
games.variants: NA longbox; later bundled with Mad Dog II and Crime Patrol in the 3DO 'Gunslinger Collection' (1995)
games.modern: No verified current digital sale; original discs and legacy Digital Leisure editions (platforms vary).
games.notes: 3DO release Jan 1994 per Wikipedia list. GameRankings avg 55%. MobyGames blocked fetching; scores unfilled.

games.title: Mad Dog II: The Lost Gold
games.alsoOn: Arcade, Sega CD, CD-i, DOS, DVD TV game, Wii, PS3/PSN
games.cast: Ben Zeller (stagecoach driver); other cast uncredited local actors
games.hook: Pick one of three guides (Buckskin Bonnie, the Professor or Shooting Beaver) and ride three different routes to the same train-and-hideout finale.
games.cheats: None known; hidden 'sand in the chest' ending appears if you finish using more than one credit
games.video: Reduced window, ~15 fps; GamePro praised it as sharper than the original — verify exact size
games.difficulty: Three difficulty levels; three lives; Gamegun strongly recommended
games.endings: Three branching routes converge on one ending; alternate 'fool's gold' chest scene if continues were used
games.trivia: The 3DO version has a single save slot and three difficulty settings. The sand-chest gag is absent from the CD-i and DVD versions.
games.modern: No verified current digital sale; original discs and legacy Digital Leisure editions (platforms vary).
games.notes: 3DO release Sept 1, 1994 (Wikipedia list). EGM 6.2/10, Next Gen 2/5.
games.criticSrc: average of 2 reviews on Wikipedia (EGM, NGen)

games.title: Crime Patrol
games.alsoOn: Arcade, Sega CD, CD-i, DOS, Mac, Windows, DVD TV game
games.hook: Rise from rookie beat cop to SWAT and Delta Force in a game that plays like a cheap 80s cop show you can shoot at.
games.video: Reduced window, ~15 fps; GamePro praised 'clean, sharp digitized images' vs the grainy Sega CD — verify size
games.difficulty: Moderate; fast enemy draws, pad cursor sluggish without Gamegun
games.endings: Linear four-tier progression (Rookie, Undercover, SWAT, Delta Force); one ending
games.trivia: Play Meter ranked the arcade original ninth in July 1993. Jaguar CD, PlayStation and Saturn ports were cancelled.
games.modern: No verified current digital sale; original discs and legacy Digital Leisure editions (platforms vary).
games.notes: Home 3DO release Nov 15, 1994 (Wikipedia 3DO list); the 1993 date in other sources is the arcade original. Single disc (ROM sets list one disc; resale listings are 'disc only').

games.title: Crime Patrol 2: Drug Wars
games.alsoOn: Arcade, CD-i, DOS, DVD TV game
games.hook: You're a DEA agent chasing a South American drug baron from New Mexico to Chicago to the jungle, with a partner who scolds you every time you die.
games.video: Reduced window; Next Gen called resolution and frame rate 'choppy' — verify size
games.difficulty: Moderate-hard; 'unplayable without a Gamegun' per Next Generation
games.endings: Four locations with three missions each, order selectable; one ending
games.trivia: ALG's seventh live-action shooter. Arcade cabinets came in 25-, 33- and 50-inch monitor sizes.
games.modern: No verified current digital sale; original discs and legacy Digital Leisure editions (platforms vary).
games.notes: 3DO release 1994 (Wikipedia list). Next Gen 2/5. Disc count unverified.

games.title: Who Shot Johnny Rock?
games.alsoOn: Arcade, Sega CD, CD-i, DOS, Windows, DVD TV game
games.hook: A 1930s gangster murder mystery where the killer is randomly picked from four suspects each playthrough and you buy bullets from a crooked doctor.
games.video: Reduced window, ~15 fps; EGM called the graphics weak for the 3DO — verify size
games.difficulty: Hard with pad; money system means a game over when cash runs out
games.endings: Randomized culprit among four gangsters; final mansion confrontation; one ending structure
games.trivia: Shown at the 1991 Las Vegas Amusement Expo as 'Who Killed Johnny Rock?'. EGM gave the 3DO port 4.8/10.
games.modern: No verified current digital sale; original discs and legacy Digital Leisure editions (platforms vary).
games.notes: 3DO release June 21, 1994 (Wikipedia list).

games.title: Space Pirates
games.cast: Ben Zeller (old man); the other actors are not named in available sources
games.hook: ALG's lone sci-fi shooter: rubber-suited pirates, a captive Commander Skye and a Star-Splitter Cannon, all with the production values of an 80s music video.
games.cheats: No codes. Secret scene: after rescuing the commander, take the transporter, choose the lower-left TV monitor and shoot the cow skull there several times. (GameFAQs)
games.video: Reduced window, ~15 fps — verify size
games.difficulty: Moderate; inaccurate targeting criticized with both pad and Gamegun
games.endings: Visit four planets in any order for three crystals, then destroy the Black Dragon; one ending
games.trivia: Ben Zeller returns from the Mad Dog games. The 3DO port supports two-player play, which the PC version lacks.
games.modern: No verified current digital sale; original discs and legacy Digital Leisure editions (platforms vary).
games.notes: 3DO release June 26, 1995 (Wikipedia list). Next Gen 2/5; Video Game Critic F.

games.title: The Last Bounty Hunter
games.alsoOn: Arcade, DOS, CD-i, DVD TV game, Wii
games.cast: Wes Flowers (fast-draw champion, as a gunfighter); others uncredited
games.hook: ALG's last Western lets you wound and capture outlaws alive for bigger bounties, with random fast-draw showdowns against a real champion.
games.video: Reduced window, ~15 fps — verify size
games.difficulty: Hard; some enemies cannot be answered in time unless you've already been shot by them
games.endings: Ending varies by whether bosses were captured alive or killed; random showdown order
games.trivia: One of the last ALG laserdisc shooters; real-life fast-draw champ Wes Flowers appears, foreshadowing Fast Draw Showdown.
games.modern: No verified current digital sale; original discs and legacy Digital Leisure editions (platforms vary).
games.notes: 3DO release Oct/Nov 1995 (sources differ). Next Gen 2/5.

games.title: Night Trap
games.source: Original production (footage shot 1987 for Hasbro's unreleased NEMO/Control-Vision VHS console)
games.alsoOn: Sega CD, 32X, DOS, Mac; Night Trap 25th Anniversary on PS4, Switch, Xbox One, PC, Vita
games.cast: Dana Plato (Kelli), Andras Jones (Jeff), Christy Ford, Debra Parks; directed by James Riley
games.cidTrigger: Theme song 'Night Trap' (Sunny Blue) may match later re-releases' audio
games.hook: The game that sparked the 1993 US Senate hearings and the ESRB, in its best-looking 1990s version with Dana Plato on a 3DO.
games.video: Larger window and far more colors than Sega CD; faster room switching; ~15 fps — verify size
games.difficulty: Hard without a walkthrough; strict trap timing and colour-code changes
games.endings: Multiple failure endings (missed Augers, missed code change, trapping a friend); one true ending
games.trivia: 3DO release has a different cover from the Sega CD original and the revised icons/fonts/'SCAT' acronym of the later ports. Dec 1993/Jan 1994 NA; June 25, 1994 in Japan.
games.variants: NA longbox, PAL, Japanese (Virgin) release; 2-disc set
games.modern: Yes (Night Trap 25th Anniversary Edition — PS4, Switch, Xbox One, Steam, Vita; Limited Run physical)
games.notes: Edge 5/10 for 3DO. Two discs (Glitchwave lists 2xCD-ROM; PriceCharting and eBay listings show Disc 1 and Disc 2). Some sources date the 3DO release Dec 1993.

games.title: Sewer Shark
games.source: Original production (footage shot 1987 for Hasbro's unreleased NEMO console)
games.cast: Robert Costanzo (Commissioner Stenchler), David Underwood (Ghost), Robert Weaver (Catfish), Kari G. Peyton (Falco); visual effects by John Dykstra
games.hook: A $3 million sci-fi sewer-tunnel shooter directed by Star Wars effects legend John Dykstra, and the 3DO is the only place to see it in full colour.
games.video: Larger video window and clearer footage than Sega CD, ~15 fps, 24-bit colour — verify size
games.difficulty: Hard; missed tube-jump calls end the game instantly
games.endings: One ending (reach Solar City); game-over death scenes from Stenchler
games.trivia: Footage was filmed in 1987 for Hasbro's NEMO VHS system; Sony first eyed it for a SNES CD add-on. The 3DO port was published by Hasbro itself.
games.notes: Video Game Critic grade C-. Exact 3DO date unknown (1994).

games.title: Corpse Killer
games.publisher: Digital Pictures / Acclaim Distribution (NA), Acclaim Japan (JP); PAL 1994 per Wikipedia list
games.source: Original production (shot on location in Jamaica-style tropical island setting)
games.alsoOn: Sega CD, 32X CD, Saturn (Graveyard Edition), Windows, Mac; Corpse Killer 25th Anniversary on PS4, Switch, PC
games.cast: Vincent Schiavelli (Dr. Hellman); live-action footage directed by John Lafia (Wikipedia)
games.peripherals: Standard control pad; 3DO Gamegun (supported but undocumented on packaging)
games.hook: Vincent Schiavelli's mad scientist and a Jamaican sidekick named Winston make this the most quotable zombie shooter of the FMV era, with secret Gamegun support on 3DO.
games.video: Larger, cleaner window than Sega CD but still grainy; ~15 fps — verify size
games.difficulty: Moderate-hard; swarming zombies drain health fast with a pad
games.trivia: The 3DO manual never mentions light-gun support, yet the Gamegun works. Japan got it on August 25, 1995 via Acclaim Japan.
games.variants: NA longbox, Japanese Acclaim release, PAL release; single disc
games.modern: Yes (Corpse Killer 25th Anniversary Edition — PS4, Switch, Steam; Limited Run physical)
games.notes: Release dating is inconsistent across sources (NA 1994 vs March 1, 1995; PAL Aug 1994; JP Aug 25, 1995). Single disc on 3DO (ROM sets list one disc, about 460 MB); the Saturn version is the 2-disc one.

games.title: Supreme Warrior
games.publisher: Digital Pictures / Acclaim Distribution (NA), Acclaim Japan (JP); EU Feb 1995 and AU Apr 1995 releases (Wikipedia)
games.source: Original production, shot on Shaw Brothers Studio sets in Hong Kong
games.cast: Vivian Wu (Wu Ching), Roger Yuan (Fang Tu), Richard Norton, Chuck Jeffreys, Ron Yuan (warlords)
games.hook: A first-person kung fu movie shot at the Shaw Brothers studios with Richard Norton, played through a stuntman's head-cam.
games.video: Roughly three-quarter-screen window, among the best video on 3DO per EGM; ~15 fps — verify size
games.difficulty: Very hard; blocking timing rarely registers
games.endings: One ending (defeat Fang Tu after four warlords); failure scenes
games.trivia: Fights were filmed with a minicam strapped to the stunt coordinator's head. The Cantonese dub is out of sync because the actors spoke English on set.
games.variants: NA longbox (Nov 1994), PAL (Feb 1995), Australia (Apr 1995), Japan (Acclaim, Aug 1995); 2-disc set
games.notes: EGM 5/10 x4, Next Gen 2/5, Video Game Critic F. Save method unverified (passwords assumed). Two discs (ROM sets list Disc 1 and 2).

games.title: Quarterback Attack with Mike Ditka
games.source: Original production (filmed over two weeks, ~$2 million budget)
games.cast: Mike Ditka (head coach); unlicensed actor players
games.hook: Mike Ditka screams at you from the sideline in a first-person FMV football game whose footage later turned up in the 2003 film Game Over.
games.video: Large window, praised video quality by GamePro; ~15 fps — verify size
games.difficulty: Moderate; read-and-react passing with a timing window
games.trivia: Asked if it was hard to bring his energy to a film crew, Ditka replied 'It's not that hard to do, really.' No NFL licence, so teams and players are fictional.
games.notes: 3DO release Nov 27, 1995. Disc count and save method unverified.

games.title: Dragon's Lair
games.alsoOn: Arcade, Sega CD, CD-i, Jaguar CD, DOS, Mac, Amiga, DVD, Blu-ray, Wii, DSiWare, iOS, PS3, Android, Switch, Steam, PS4, Xbox
games.cast: Don Bluth (director/animator), Dan Molina (Dirk), Vera Lanpher-Pacheco (Daphne)
games.cidTrigger: Dragon's Lair animation/score matched by Digital Leisure's many re-releases
games.hook: Don Bluth's 1983 laserdisc classic finally in near-full-screen colour on a console, if you can tolerate the input lag.
games.cheats: Unlimited lives: at the title press Up, Down, Left, Right, Up, Down, Left, Right. View every scene: lose all lives, then on the continue screen press Right, Right, Left, Left, Down, Down, Up, Up, P. (GameFAQs)
games.video: Near full-screen (letterboxed) Cinepak video at reduced frame rate (~12-15 fps vs 24); input response laggy — verify
games.difficulty: Hard; memorisation-based with sluggish move windows
games.endings: Linear with random room order; one ending (rescue Daphne)
games.trivia: Japan got the 3DO version first (T&E Soft, March 1994). A Dragon's Lair II 3DO port was announced but only survives as a non-playable demo on Brain Dead 13's 3DO disc.
games.variants: NA longbox (June 1994), PAL, Japanese T&E Soft release
games.modern: Yes (Dragon's Lair Trilogy — Steam, Switch, PS4, Xbox; Arcade1Up)
games.notes: Wikipedia main article has no 3DO detail; dates from the List of 3DO games.

games.title: Space Ace
games.alsoOn: Arcade, Amiga, ST, Apple IIGS, DOS, Mac, Sega CD, CD-i, Jaguar CD, DVD, Blu-ray, Wii, DSiWare, iOS, PS3, Android, Switch, Steam
games.cast: Don Bluth (director); voices incl. Michael Rye (narrator)
games.cidTrigger: Space Ace animation/score matched by Digital Leisure re-releases
games.hook: Bluth's second laserdisc epic lets you transform between Ace and Dexter mid-scene, but the 3DO port dropped animation frames and got harder for it.
games.cheats: GameFAQs lists no 3DO-specific codes. On the Sega CD version, pausing and pressing Right, Right, Left, Left, Down, Down, Up, Up, Start makes the game self-play; untested on 3DO. (GameFAQs)
games.video: Near full-screen Cinepak video with dropped frames (Video Game Critic); ~12-15 fps — verify
games.difficulty: Very hard; memorisation with poor input response
games.endings: Branching Ace/Dexter scene choices; one ending (defeat Borf)
games.trivia: Released late in the 3DO's life (July 1995) with no PAL or Japanese release, making it one of the rarer ReadySoft 3DO discs.
games.modern: Yes (Dragon's Lair Trilogy — Steam, Switch, PS4, Xbox)
games.notes: Video Game Critic D-. Wikipedia main article has no 3DO detail.

shots.title: All 4 of the floppy disks for the Atari ST version of the game 'Space Ace' taken using Cannon Power Shot S3

games.title: Brain Dead 13
games.alsoOn: DOS, Windows, Mac, PlayStation, Saturn, Jaguar CD, CD-i, iOS
games.cast: Voices: Riccardo Durante (Lance), Dave Quesnelle (Dr. Neurosis), Joe Giampapa (Fritz), June Brown (Vivi), Blayne Burnside (Moose)
games.hook: A Dragon's Lair-style cartoon made in Toronto, with Fritz the deranged mascot and the best video of any version thanks to a two-disc 3DO release.
games.video: Near full-screen, higher quality than PC/Saturn/Jaguar single-disc versions; ~15 fps — verify
games.difficulty: Hard; unlimited lives but trial-and-error death scenes
games.endings: Non-linear castle exploration; one ending (defeat Dr. Neurosis)
games.trivia: Disc 1 exists in an original and a v1.1 pressing that fixes a crash in Vivi's salon. The disc also carries a non-playable Dragon's Lair II 3DO demo.
games.variants: NA longbox; Disc 1 original vs v1.1 revision
games.modern: No verified current digital sale; historical iOS edition and original discs.
games.notes: 3DO release Dec 15, 1995 (or 1996 per main article). EGM 9/7.5/7/7, AllGame 3.5/5.

games.title: Strahl
games.alt: Triad Stone (LaserActive); シュトラール (JP)
games.developer: Data East / Media Entertainment; animation by Toei Animation
games.source: Pioneer LaserActive Mega-LD game Triad Stone (1993), itself from a shelved 1985 laserdisc arcade project 'Chantze's Stone'
games.alsoOn: Pioneer LaserActive (as Triad Stone), Sega Saturn
games.hook: A lost 1985 Toei anime laserdisc game resurrected a decade later, with a 'Power! Power! Power!' button-mashing gimmick.
games.video: Full-screen animation, 'on par with old Japanese cartoons like Speed Racer' (Video Game Critic); ~15 fps — verify
games.difficulty: Easy per EGM; no difficulty select on 3DO
games.trivia: The 3DO version has a unique intro and stage-select art and omits the extra action sequences added to the Saturn version.
games.variants: Japanese Media Entertainment release (Dec 1994), NA Panasonic longbox (July 1995)
games.notes: EGM 6.125/10, Next Gen 1/5, Video Game Critic C.

games.title: Star Wars: Rebel Assault
games.publisher: LucasArts (NA), Electronic Arts (EU), Electronic Arts Victor (JP)
games.source: PC original (MS-DOS, Nov 1993); Star Wars film license
games.cast: No film cast; new actors as Rookie One and Rebel pilots; digitized film footage and John Williams score
games.cidTrigger: John Williams Star Wars score and digitized clips from the original trilogy throughout
games.hook: The CD-ROM-era killer app that put you in a Star Wars movie, ported to the console built for exactly this.
games.cheats: Console ports give a password after every level; PC-only cheats (damage control, ending) — 3DO codes unverified
games.video: Close port of the PC version; low-res pre-rendered video scaled near full screen with sprite overlays, roughly 15 fps (verify)
games.difficulty: Moderate; three difficulty settings, controls widely criticised as imprecise
games.endings: Linear 15-chapter story; each chapter has a short 'alternate ending' death clip when lives run out
games.trivia: Sold around 1 million copies across platforms and is credited with accelerating CD-ROM adoption. A physical Star Destroyer model was digitised for one mission.
games.variants: NA (LucasArts), PAL (EA), Japanese (EA Victor) releases; later NA reprints in slim case (verify)
games.modern: No (3DO version); PC version sold on Steam/GOG via Disney/LucasArts
games.notes: 3DO dates per Wikipedia 3DO list: NA Dec 1, 1994; JP Feb 17, 1995; PAL 1994. Next Generation gave the 3DO port 2/5.

games.title: Microcosm
games.alsoOn: FM Towns, Sega CD, Amiga CD32, MS-DOS
games.cast: Rick Wakeman (Yes) composed the soundtrack
games.cidTrigger: Rick Wakeman soundtrack could be fingerprinted if ever released commercially
games.hook: Fantastic Voyage as a shooter: fly through a human body over SGI-rendered video that looked like the future and played like a slideshow.
games.video: Pre-rendered Cinepak-style video in a sub-full-screen window, around 12–15 fps; big step up from Sega CD
games.difficulty: Hard and frustrating; Next Generation called it 'never challenging, only frustrating'
games.trivia: Computer Gaming World named its backstory the worst of all time in 1996. First of a loose Psygnosis trilogy with Novastorm (Scavenger 4) and the Japan-only MegaMorph.
games.variants: NA Psygnosis long box; Japanese T&E Soft release
games.notes: 3DO NA Mar 14, 1994; JP Jul 9, 1994; no PAL 3DO release per Wikipedia list. EGM 4/10 unanimous.

games.title: Novastorm
games.source: Original production (FM Towns original as Scavenger 4)
games.alsoOn: FM Towns, Sega CD, MS-DOS, PlayStation
games.hook: Psygnosis' second pre-rendered rail shooter, gorgeous and hollow, with a 3DO Shooter of the Year award to its name.
games.cheats: DOS 'TOMATOES' code; 3DO codes unverified — None known
games.video: Windowed pre-rendered video (only PlayStation got full screen), roughly 15 fps
games.difficulty: Easy; GamePro found it lacking intensity
games.trivia: Won GameFan's 1994 Best 3DO Shooter award. Obstacles in the pre-rendered backdrop can actually damage the ship, unlike most video-backdrop shooters.
games.variants: NA Psygnosis release; Japanese T&E Soft release as Scavenger 4
games.notes: 3DO JP Oct 7, 1994; NA Dec 15, 1994; no PAL 3DO. EGM 5/10, Next Generation 1/5.

games.title: MegaRace
games.publisher: Mindscape / The Software Toolworks (NA, EU), Multisoft (JP)
games.cast: Christian Erickson as host Lance Boyle
games.hook: Sleazy game-show host Lance Boyle mocks you between races on pre-rendered tracks — the most quotable FMV ham of the era.
games.video: Pre-rendered track video with sprite cars, near full screen; Lance Boyle live-action segments ~20 min total
games.trivia: Over twenty minutes of Lance Boyle footage. An Amiga CD32 version was announced but never released.
games.variants: NA Mindscape long box; PAL release; Japanese Multisoft release
games.modern: No (3DO); PC version on GOG since 2009
games.notes: 3DO NA May 1994; JP Oct 7, 1994; PAL 1994. Next Generation 4/5 for 3DO.

games.title: D
games.alt: D no Shokutaku (JP); D's Diner: Director's Cut (JP re-release)
games.cast: Kenji Eno (director); 'digital actress' Laura; Japanese voice cast
games.hook: Kenji Eno smuggled cannibalism past the censors by swapping master discs on the plane — and the 3DO got a genuine Japanese hit.
games.video: Full-screen pre-rendered Amiga 4000 CG video, roughly 15 fps; among the best-looking 3DO FMV
games.difficulty: Moderate; strict two-hour real-time limit with no pause or save
games.endings: Multiple endings depending on actions (e.g. shooting Laura's father vs. approaching him)
games.trivia: Eno submitted a clean version for approval then swapped in violent masters en route to the US manufacturer. D's Diner Director's Cut (JP, Jan 1996) added content and a soundtrack disc.
games.variants: JP original (San-ei Shobo), JP Director's Cut 3-disc set with soundtrack, NA Panasonic release, PAL release
games.modern: No (3DO); DOS version on Steam/GOG via Nightdive (2016)
games.notes: JP Apr 1, 1995 (San-Ei Shobo); NA 1995 (Panasonic). Wikipedia's game infobox lists no PAL 3DO release, though the 3DO list gives PAL 1995. GameFan 1995 3DO Game of the Year.

games.title: Creature Shock
games.hook: Argonaut's gigabyte-sized pre-rendered alien hunt arrived on 3DO late, slow and ugly-mean — a perfect 'too late' story.
games.cheats: Saturn/PS level-skip codes exist; 3DO codes unverified — None known
games.video: Pre-rendered video, three FMV exploration levels and two rail-shooter levels; slow cursor, modest frame rate
games.difficulty: Hard; single weapon and sluggish cursor
games.trivia: A Jaguar CD port was shown at E3 1995 and cancelled after a poor reception. The full game exceeded a gigabyte across two discs.
games.notes: 3DO NA Mar 19, 1996; no JP/PAL 3DO per Wikipedia list. GamePro negative on 3DO.

games.title: Cyberia
