games.alsoOn: MS-DOS, Mac, Windows, Sega Saturn, PlayStation, FM Towns, PC-98, Linux
games.hook: Motion-captured pre-rendered cyberpunk with one-shot deaths every thirty seconds — the Dragon's Lair of the 3D era.
games.cheats: No 3DO codes listed (the PlayStation version has passwords). The 3DO Flightstick Pro works in the arcade sequences although the game never says so. (GameFAQs)
games.video: Pre-rendered gameplay and cutscenes near full screen; Next Generation said all four console/PC versions were 'exactly' alike
games.trivia: Reportedly one of the first pre-rendered games to use motion capture. An OEM cut, Cyberia: Mission Norway, shipped with sound cards.
games.variants: PAL Interplay release (1994/95), NA Interplay release (1996), Japanese EA Victor release (1996)
games.notes: Wikipedia list gives PAL Nov 1, 1994, NA Feb 12, 1996, JP Jan 26, 1996 — PAL-first date flagged 'citation needed'; verify.

games.title: Lost Eden
games.cast: Stéphane Picq (composer)
games.hook: Cryo's dinosaurs-and-humans fable with a cult Stéphane Picq soundtrack — one of the few 3DO adventures critics actually liked.
games.video: Pre-rendered panning backgrounds and CG cutscenes, near full screen
games.trivia: Written with Steve Jackson (Fighting Fantasy). Next Generation gave the 3DO version 4/5, EGM 7.625/10.
games.variants: NA Virgin release; PAL 3DO release unconfirmed
games.notes: 3DO NA Mar 1, 1995; JP/PAL listed unreleased on Wikipedia — verify PAL.

games.title: Dragon Lore: The Legend Begins
games.hook: A three-disc pre-rendered fantasy quest where dying in a cutscene was half the appeal.
games.video: Pre-rendered animation sequences, near full screen; slow disc access noted by GamePro
games.endings: Single main ending with multiple death sequences
games.trivia: Sold 300,000 units by 1997 and was bundled with the Reveal multimedia kit alongside MegaRace.
games.variants: NA Mindscape 3-disc long box; PAL release 1995
games.notes: 3DO NA Oct 30, 1995; PAL 1995; no JP. GamePro brief positive review May 1996.

games.title: Myst
games.alsoOn: Mac, Windows, Saturn, PlayStation, Jaguar CD, CD-i, PSP, DS, 3DS, iOS, Android, Switch, VR
games.cast: Rand Miller as Atrus, Robyn Miller as Sirrus, Chuck Carter as Achenar
games.hook: The game that sold CD-ROM drives, on the console that needed it most — a near-identical port with a controller cursor.
games.video: Pre-rendered stills with small QuickTime-style video insets of live actors; full-screen 320x240 scenes
games.difficulty: Moderate to hard; pure puzzle logic, no deaths
games.endings: Four endings: trapped with Sirrus, with Achenar, trapped in D'ni with Atrus, or the true ending
games.trivia: Wikipedia credits Sunsoft for NA in one note, Panasonic elsewhere — the NA 3DO box is Panasonic. GamePro gave the 3DO port a perfect 5/5 across categories.
games.variants: NA Panasonic long box, PAL Panasonic, Japanese Microcabin release
games.modern: No (3DO); numerous remakes/re-releases on PC, consoles, mobile and VR
games.notes: 3DO NA Mar 17, 1995; JP Apr 14, 1995; PAL 1995. Next Generation 2/5.

games.title: The Daedalus Encounter
games.cast: Tia Carrere as Ariel Matheson, Christian Bocher as Zack Smith
games.hook: You are a brain in a jar and Tia Carrere is your pilot — four discs of full-screen sci-fi FMV, the 3DO's showcase port.
games.video: Video always full screen on 3DO (PC used a windowed interface); praised as the best-looking version
games.endings: Three endings: Artemis burns up; Ari kills the alien Queen and escapes; or the alien responds to Casey and repairs the ship
games.trivia: Alternate scenes were filmed at Cinerent Stage A in San Francisco so the story shifts with player progress. Maximum called the 3DO FMV 'by far the most superior effort of any format.'
games.variants: NA Panasonic 4-disc long box; PAL Panasonic; Japanese Hatnet release
games.notes: 3DO NA Sep 30, 1995; JP Nov 10, 1995; PAL 1995. Next Generation 3/5.

games.title: Psychic Detective
games.source: Original production (PC and 3DO released close together, late 1995)
games.cast: Kevin Breznahan as Eric Fox, Beata Pozniak as Laina Pozok
games.length: 45 min per run; multiple runs needed
games.hook: A 45-minute psychic noir you can replay a dozen ways — including by doing nothing at all.
games.video: Live-action video near full screen with clickable icons; GamePro praised its sharp FMV on 3DO
games.difficulty: Easy per run; the challenge is finding branches
games.endings: About a dozen endings; the finale is a surreal board game against the villain
games.trivia: About 200 people worked on it, including 95 actors; shot over 20 days in San Francisco and Oakland. The footage was cut into a short film shown at a film festival.
games.variants: NA EA 3-disc long box; PAL release 1995/96
games.notes: 3DO NA date conflicts: Wikipedia 3DO list and retail listings give Nov 10, 1995; the Wikipedia article and GameFAQs say 1996. PAL 1995. Three discs (ROM sets list Disc 1 to 3 of 3).

games.title: Hell: A Cyberpunk Thriller
games.cast: Dennis Hopper, Grace Jones, Stephanie Seymour, Geoffrey Holder
games.hook: Dennis Hopper and Grace Jones voice CG demons in a 2095 theocratic Washington — and the 3DO runs the whole thing full screen.
games.video: Same FMV as PC but played entirely full screen (PC was partial-screen); rendered characters over live/CG backdrops
games.difficulty: Hard; pixel-hunting cursor and script bugs can make puzzles unsolvable
games.trivia: Sold 300,000 units in six months, yet CGW named it the 12th-worst computer game ever in 1996. Chet Williamson wrote a novelization.
games.variants: NA GameTek long box; Wikipedia's game infobox gives an EU 1994 release for MS-DOS/3DO, which the 3DO list omits.
games.modern: No (not sold on GOG or Steam)
games.notes: 3DO NA Dec 1994. Single disc per PriceCharting listings. Next Generation 2/5 for 3DO.

games.title: Snow Job
games.cast: Tracy Scoggins
games.hook: One of the very last 3DO releases: a mob-noir FMV mystery with Tracy Scoggins that sold so badly sealed copies now fetch four figures.
games.video: Live-action video over 360-degree photorealistic pre-rendered environments, near full screen
games.trivia: Published by The 3DO Company itself at the very end of the platform's life in May 1996 and sold poorly, making it one of the rarer NA releases. GamePro compared Psychic Detective favourably to it.
games.variants: NA Studio 3DO 2-disc long box; PAL release listed as 1996 — verify
games.notes: 3DO NA May 15, 1996 per Wikipedia list; MobyGames critic 66% (3 ratings), player 3.4/5. Disc count from eBay/PriceCharting listings (2-disc set).

games.title: Twisted: The Game Show
games.alt: Twisted (JP: Twisted: The Game Show, EA Victor)
games.source: Original production (3DO launch-window title, directed/designed by Jim Eisenstein; produced by Stewart Bonn and Trip Hawkins)
games.cast: Tohoru Masamune (Johnny Pow; later Shredder in 2014 TMNT); other actors play Humble Howard, Major Steel, Madame Elaine, Wormington, host Twink Fizzdale and assistant Hannah; Uncle Fez is CGI
games.peripherals: Standard 3DO controller; up to 4 players via daisy-chained pads
games.cidTrigger: Public-domain/stock footage (nuclear test clips, old films) in Zapper and Mystery Matinee minigames; original music by Ed Bogas/Gary Clayton/Joe Buzcek
games.hook: A 3DO launch-era parody game show where six daytime-TV stereotypes race up a 90-space helix while unskippable fake commercials play — it is the 3DO's house style distilled.
games.video: Partial-screen live-action windows over computer-drawn sets, roughly 15 fps Cinepak-era quality; some minigame clips are black-and-white
games.difficulty: Low; trivia has three selectable difficulty levels or can be turned off
games.endings: No story; the first player to the top of the helix wins
games.trivia: Sequel Zhadnost: The People's Party followed in 1995 from the same director. EGM scored it 8.2/10 and Entertainment Weekly gave an A-; JP release came 23 Dec 1994.
games.variants: NA long-box (1993/1994 reprints), EA Victor JP release, PAL EA release
games.notes: NA date variously listed as late 1993 or 15 Apr 1994 (Wikipedia list). JP publisher EA Victor. Non-active players must watch everyone else's clips, so matches drag.

games.title: Zhadnost: The People's Party
games.alt: The All New People's Game Show (working title)
games.source: Original production; sequel to Twisted, again designed and directed by Jim Eisenstein
games.cast: Live-action cast as the Soviet-parody host and contestants (names not widely documented — verify); CG art direction by Kurt Kaufman
games.peripherals: Standard 3DO controller; multiplayer via daisy-chained pads
games.cidTrigger: Original soundtrack by George 'The Fat Man' Sanger (released on his album Surf.com) — unlikely to be claimed
games.hook: A Soviet-themed game show parody ('Zhadnost' means greed) with a Fat Man soundtrack — one of the strangest things 3DO ever published in-house.
games.video: Live-action contestants composited into CG sets, partial-screen windows, ~15 fps
games.difficulty: Low; simple contests, wears thin quickly per Next Generation
games.trivia: Announced in early 1995 as The All New People's Game Show. One of the few 3DO exclusives with a commercial soundtrack release (Sanger's Surf.com). Edge gave it 3/10 while GamePro gave 17.5/20.
games.notes: Kaufman called it 'somewhat experimental' for a period when 3DO focused on fighting/shooting/sports.

games.title: Family Feud
games.alsoOn: Separate GameTek versions on SNES, Genesis, PC and others (different code)
games.cast: Wal Foster appears in digitized footage as the Richard Dawson-lookalike host; Ron Beuhrer provides host voice-over
games.cidTrigger: Family Feud theme music and licensed show presentation (Fremantle/Sony owns the format and theme)
games.hook: The first Family Feud with a voiced, digitized host — a lookalike playing Richard Dawson on a console nobody bought.
games.cheats: None known (TCRF lists unused early set graphics and an unused theme variant, no debug mode)
games.video: Small digitized host clips over a drawn set, low frame rate
games.endings: No story; win or lose the Fast Money round
games.trivia: First Feud game with a voiced host and one of the few to include the Bullseye round. Next Generation gave it 3/5, saying enjoyment depends on liking the TV show.
games.notes: Wikipedia list gives 1993/1994; TCRF gives 6 May 1994. Developer Eurocom per TCRF/Wikipedia list.

games.title: Dennis Miller: That's News to Me
games.alt: Dennis Miller's That's News To Me (I-Laugh series)
games.source: Original production — stand-up/news-desk monologues by comedian Dennis Miller, part of Sanctuary Woods' I-Laugh line
games.cast: Dennis Miller
games.cidTrigger: Dennis Miller's comedy material is copyrighted performance content; possible claim by rights holders of the recorded routines
games.hook: Not a game at all: a disc of Dennis Miller riffing on 1994 headlines, sorted by category — the 3DO as a comedy jukebox.
games.video: Windowed live-action clips, roughly 15 fps; jokes sometimes cut off awkwardly
games.difficulty: N/A — pick a category and watch
games.trivia: Wikipedia's 3DO list files it in the non-game table with a 31 Dec 1994 date. The Video Game Critic gave it an F, noting many jokes are dated and fall flat without an audience.
games.variants: NA jewel/long-box; Digital Game Museum holds the box (2012.013.079)
games.notes: Companion title Dennis Miller: Geek to Me was PC-only. Exact NA release date uncertain.

games.title: Plumbers Don't Wear Ties
games.source: Original production (writer/director/producer Michael Anderson); tiny 1993 Windows release preceded 3DO
games.alsoOn: Windows (1993, very limited); PS4/PS5/Switch/Xbox/PC re-release (Limited Run Games, 2024); ScummVM
games.cast: Edward J. Foster (John), Jeanne Basone (Jane; ex-GLOW wrestler 'Hollywood'), Paul Bokor (Thresher), Michael Anderson (narrator/Harry Armis), Thyra Metz (narrator Wilma)
games.cidTrigger: Original score by Martin Golnick; no licensed material
games.hook: Advertised as full-motion video but delivered as a slideshow with two bickering narrators — routinely called the worst game ever made, and now a cult object with a 2024 remaster.
games.cheats: Special mode: while the girl is talking at the start, press Up, Down, Right, Left, Down, Right, X. (GameFAQs) Whether this is the uncensored mode isn't stated.
games.video: Primarily a narrated still-photo slideshow; the 3DO edition has a filmed introduction. Not mostly full-motion video.
games.difficulty: Trivial; wrong picks just trigger narrator abuse and a retry
games.endings: Branching with several fail endings (Jane with Thresher, Jane as prostitute, Jane as nun) plus the 'good' dinner ending
games.trivia: PC version was thought lost until a copy surfaced at Ball State University in 2017. EGM named it 4th worst console game ever (1997); AVGN covered it in 2009.
games.variants: NA 3DO long-box (30 Sep 1994); Limited Run physical editions and a novelization by Mike Drucker (2024)
games.modern: No (3DO); Definitive Edition sold on GOG, PS4/PS5, Switch and Xbox
games.notes: Retained as a culturally relevant adjacent title in the broad index; excluded from the strict FMV audit because gameplay uses still photographs. Definitive Edition is sold on GOG and modern consoles.

games.title: Station Invasion
games.source: Original production; edutainment commissioned by Trip Hawkins, ~8.5-month development
games.cast: Child actors as Billy, Angelica, Bryce, Sopha Sinfree and Ernie; a Golden Retriever in a suit as newscaster John (actor names undocumented — verify)
games.peripherals: Standard 3DO controller; up to 5 players sharing one pad
games.cidTrigger: Original music; tile puzzles use public-domain fine art
games.hook: Kids seize a TV station and you earn ratings by doing math and word puzzles between live-action sketches — Ed Rotberg (Battlezone) making edutainment for 3DO.
games.cheats: None known; FMV can be skipped or turned off entirely in options
games.video: Live-action kids composited into CG sets, windowed, ~15 fps; short show clips play as rewards
games.difficulty: Four selectable difficulty levels; aimed at under-8s per Next Generation
games.endings: No story; highest ratings after 'Sweeps Week' wins and an awards-ceremony clip plays
games.trivia: Rotberg said the game was 'not as big a success as we would have liked' and that DVD-sized storage would have made a much better version. Next Generation: 'If you're under eight, it's a scream.'
games.variants: NA (6 Dec 1994) and PAL (1994) releases under the Club 3DO label
games.notes: Reviews: Game Players 75%, Next Gen 3/5, 3DO Magazine 3/5, Electronic Games D+.

games.title: Cowboy Casino
games.source: Original production — poker coaching title from Atlanta's Intellimedia (ESPN instructional-video licensee)
games.cast: Unnamed actors as five Old West opponents (cowboy, gambler, dude, bandito, miner) and a card-counting bartender
games.cidTrigger: Original saloon music; no licensed content
games.hook: Five filmed saloon caricatures react to every hand you play — an FMV poker tutor that MAN!AC crowned 'Flop of the Year'.
games.video: Windowed live-action reaction clips over a static table, ~15 fps
games.difficulty: Low to medium; critics doubted the dealing was fair
games.endings: None; four poker variants (5-card draw, 5-card stud, 7-card stud, Texas hold'em)
games.trivia: Bundled with J. Edward Allen's booklet The Basics of Winning Poker. Giant Bomb lists Panasonic Interactive Media as publisher, conflicting with Wikipedia (IntelliPlay); Wikipedia's 3DO list dates it 21 Jul 1995 while the article says 1994.
games.variants: NA release; later PC/Mac MPC version
games.notes: Release year uncertain: 1994 (article) vs 21 Jul 1995 (list). Reviews: Entertainment Weekly B-, MAN!AC 13%, NGamer 1/5.

games.title: Kingdom: The Far Reaches
games.developer: Virtual Image Productions / Interplay (from RDI Video Systems' animation)
games.source: Arcade/Halcyon laserdisc game Thayer's Quest (RDI, 1984), re-edited with new voice-over, renamed characters and added animation/puzzles
games.alsoOn: PC (DOS), CD-i; GOG/Epic re-release of PC version; sequel Kingdom II: Shadoan (PC/CD-i, 1996)
games.cast: Voice cast undocumented — verify; original Thayer's Quest animation team under Rick Dyer
games.cidTrigger: Original score; no licensed material
games.hook: A 1984 laserdisc fantasy cartoon resurrected as a 1995 point-and-click where one wrong item use can permanently lose the game — Dragon's Lair's forgotten cousin.
games.video: Near full-screen streamed cel animation, ~15 fps, visibly pixelated
games.difficulty: High trial-and-error; limited lives and unwinnable states
games.endings: Branching dialogue and paths; one true ending (collecting three of five relics) plus many death animations
games.trivia: Thayer became Lathan Kandor and villain Sorsabal became Torlock. Kingdom II reportedly cost over $3 million with 300+ animators; a third part was never made after bankruptcy.
games.modern: Yes (PC version on GOG and Epic Games Store; 3DO version not re-released)
games.notes: Critics compared the FMV to a Saturday-morning cartoon; GamePro found it less linear than Dragon's Lair.
games.criticSrc: average of 2 reviews on Wikipedia (Maximum, NGen)

games.title: Pyramid Intruder
games.alt: Pyramid Patrol (LaserActive original); ピラミッド・イントルーダー
games.source: Remake of Taito's Pioneer LaserActive launch title Pyramid Patrol (1993), whose 3DCG footage came from a Taito motion-ride attraction
games.cidTrigger: Original Taito music
games.hook: A Japan-only 3DO remake of a LaserActive ride-film shooter: your ship flies through pre-rendered Martian pyramids Rebel Assault-style.
games.video: Near full-screen pre-rendered CG streams, ~15 fps, reworked and extended from the LaserActive footage
games.difficulty: Medium; limited movement over fixed flight path
games.trivia: The 3DO version switches from LaserActive's cursor-shooting to third-person ship control, reworks most FMV and adds new scenes. Released 11 Aug 1995, among the last Japanese 3DO titles.
games.notes: Story set in 2035: a pyramid on Mars awakens a hibernating Atlantean race. Not listed on PriceCharting.

games.title: Ultraman Powered
games.alt: ウルトラマンパワード (based on Ultraman: The Ultimate Hero)
games.source: TV license — Tsuburaya's 1993 US-made tokusatsu series Ultraman: The Ultimate Hero (Ultraman Powered)
games.alsoOn: 3DO exclusive (a different Ultraman Powered game exists on Bandai Playdia)
games.cast: Footage of the series cast (Kane Kosugi as Kenichi Kai) in FMV clips; suit actors as Ultraman and kaiju
games.cidTrigger: Extensive TV-series footage and music owned by Tsuburaya Productions
games.hook: A Japanese 3DO launch title that cuts the 1993 Los Angeles-made Ultraman show into a slow fighting game with digitized kaiju and a rail-shooter warm-up.
games.cheats: None known; versus roster unlocks by play
games.video: Windowed FMV clips from the series between bouts, ~15 fps; digitized sprites and backgrounds
games.endings: Single ending in Battle Mode; Visual Mode is three matches with long FMV
games.trivia: Released 20 Mar 1994 as a Japanese 3DO launch title. Famitsu scores ranged 5–8; Next Generation 2/5, but GameFan's Dave Halverson praised it.
games.notes: Three modes: Visual (FMV-heavy), Battle (rail shooter then fight), Versus. Japanese 3DO launch title, Mar 20, 1994. Not listed on PriceCharting.

games.title: Killing Time
games.developer: Studio 3DO (Larry Reed, Rebecca Heineman, Al Tofanelli)
games.source: Original production; 1930s Maine island mansion modeled on Boldt Castle
games.alsoOn: Windows (1996) and Mac (1997) by Logicware; GOG/ZOOM; Killing Time: Resurrected (Nightdive, 2024) on Switch/PS4/PS5/Xbox/PC
games.cast: Lise Bruneau (Tess Conway), Eric Flom, Colin Thomson, Tim Flanagan, Edward Sarafian, Paula Sonenberg, Ashley Penrod; Bruce Robertson (player voice)
games.cidTrigger: Original score by Robert Vieira
games.hook: Doom meets The 7th Guest: translucent live-action ghosts replay a 1932 party in real time inside a seamless, load-free 3DO island.
games.cheats: GameFAQs lists cheat codes only for the PC and Mac versions; none for 3DO. A Game Guru save patch fixes the clown-stage glitch.
games.video: Live-action ghost clips chroma-keyed into the 3D engine during play; full-screen FMV only for intro/ending, ~15 fps
games.difficulty: Medium-hard; big nonlinear map, button combos for weapon switching
games.trivia: Original pressing was a red disc with a clown-stage pixelation bug; 3DO mailed out a fixed black disc, which is now the rare one. Acclaim bought PS1/Saturn rights in 1996 but never shipped them.
games.variants: NA red-disc first print and black-disc fixed reprint; PAL (10 Nov 1995); JP (22 Dec 1995)
games.modern: Yes (Killing Time: Resurrected, Nightdive 2024, merging 3DO and PC assets; original PC on GOG)
games.notes: Won 3DO Adventure Game of the Year; GamesMaster ranked it #2 3DO game in 1996. Next Generation 4/5.

games.title: Wing Commander III: Heart of the Tiger
games.source: PC original (Origin, Dec 1994); 3DO conversion with added cutscenes
games.alsoOn: PC (DOS), PlayStation (1996); cancelled Jaguar CD and Saturn ports
games.cast: Mark Hamill, Malcolm McDowell, John Rhys-Davies, Tom Wilson, Jason Bernard, Ginger Lynn Allen, Josh Lucas, Courtney Gains, François Chau, Tim Curry (voice)
games.cidTrigger: Original George Oldziey score; EA/Origin footage occasionally matched by automated claims
games.hook: Mark Hamill and Malcolm McDowell star in the $4M green-screen space opera that EGM said had the cleanest FMV on any platform — and the 3DO cut adds scenes the PC never had.
games.cheats: Debug mode: at the New Game/Continue menu, hold L and P. (GameFAQs)
games.video: Near full-screen live-action composited over digital sets, sharper with fewer artifacts than PC but lower resolution; ~15 fps
games.difficulty: Fixed at roughly PC 'Veteran'; missions faster and more arcade-like than PC
games.endings: Branching romance (Flint/Rachel/neither) and Hobbes choice; only two of PC's three endings reachable on 3DO because planetary missions were cut
games.trivia: Planetary surface missions and manual takeoffs were replaced with FMV; new scenes include civilian news segments and a Hobbes hologram. Won 3DO Interactive Movie of the Year 1995.
games.modern: Yes (PC version on GOG since 2011; 3DO version not re-released)
games.notes: A 3DO-only bug marks the first Hyperion mission failed unless every enemy dies. Next Gen 5/5, EGM 7.5/10, AllGame 4/5.

games.title: Super Wing Commander
games.publisher: Origin Systems (NA), Electronic Arts (EU), Electronic Arts Victor (JP)
games.source: PC original Wing Commander (1990) plus Secret Missions, remade with redrawn art, full speech and a new 'Secret Missions 1.5' campaign
games.cast: Full voice cast (uncredited — verify); no live actors
games.cidTrigger: Original score
games.hook: The first Wing Commander rebuilt for 3DO with fully voiced, redrawn animated cutscenes — the bridge between the sprite original and WC3's movie-star FMV.
games.cheats: None known on 3DO (PC original had 'Origin -k' invulnerability)
games.video: In-engine animated cutscenes with digitized voices rather than streamed video; redrawn Tiger's Claw bar/briefing scenes
games.difficulty: Medium; branching mission tree by performance
games.endings: Winning and losing campaign tracks as in the original
games.trivia: Released 23 Mar 1994 for 3DO and Mac; includes a new third campaign and backstory on Tolwyn and stealth fighters. GamePro was negative; many fans dislike the redesigned ships.
games.variants: NA (May 1994), JP EA Victor (9 Jul 1994), PAL EA (1994)
games.modern: No (original PC Wing Commander on GOG)
games.notes: FMV content is minimal — animated, not streamed; included for completeness as WC3's predecessor.

games.title: Demolition Man
games.publisher: Virgin Interactive (NA/EU/JP; JP release Dec 9, 1994 per Wikipedia)
games.genre: Light-gun shooter / fighting / FPS / racing hybrid
games.source: Film license (Demolition Man, 1993) made in tandem with the movie, with extra Stallone and Snipes footage shot for the game
games.alsoOn: Different games on SNES, Genesis, Sega CD; Jaguar CD and PlayStation versions cancelled
games.cast: Sylvester Stallone, Wesley Snipes (exclusive footage); Jesse Ventura reportedly reprises his minion role
games.cidTrigger: Warner Bros. film footage and the movie's soundtrack used directly
games.hook: Stallone filmed new scenes just for this disc — including telling you 'you suck' for picking easy — in a 16-level grab-bag of gun, fighting, maze and driving stages.
games.cheats: Debug mode: pause (P), then press LS, A, Up, Down, RS, Up; the password ends in PWR. B+Up/Down scrolls passwords: VRGN 1 to VRGN 5 open five secret Doom-style levels set in Virgin's offices; GMWNNR shows the winning scene, CRDTS the credits. (FMV World)
games.video: Windowed movie clips plus full-screen gallery backgrounds, ~15 fps Cinepak-grade
games.difficulty: Three difficulty modes; fighting stages criticized for delayed attacks
games.trivia: Won Die Hard Game Fan's 1994 Movie Translation Game of the Year; Next Generation gave it 2/5. 9 gun levels, 4 Phoenix fights, 2 FPS mazes, 1 driving level.
games.notes: Wikipedia's 3DO infobox credits Virgin Interactive and Alexandria as developers and Virgin as publisher, JP Dec 9, 1994 and NA 1995.

games.title: Phoenix 3
games.cast: Unnamed live actors composited into pre-rendered sets as pilot Derek Freeman and crew — verify
games.peripherals: Standard controller; 3DO Flightstick Pro in space segments
games.cidTrigger: Original music
games.hook: Gray Matter's 3DO swan song alternates cockpit dogfights with Earthworm Jim-style platforming, glued together by digitized actors inside CG sets — and level data streamed inside the video.
games.cheats: Hold RS at title and enter Up, Up, Down, Down, Left, Left, Right, Right for cheat menu (invincibility, all guns, gravity, psychedelic mode); Hold RS, Down, Up, Left, Left, Up, Down, Down, Right shows hidden credits
games.video: Windowed live-action over pre-rendered backgrounds, ~15 fps
games.trivia: Programmer Stefan Posthuma interleaved level data into the FMV stream so levels loaded during cutscenes, which meant videos could not be skipped. Never ported elsewhere.
games.notes: Publisher shown as both The 3DO Company and Studio 3DO on databases; sparse review coverage.

games.title: Panzer General
games.source: PC original (SSI, 1994); console port with archival WWII newsreel footage
games.cidTrigger: Archival WWII newsreel clips and martial music in intro/briefings — mostly public domain but occasionally matched
games.hook: A faithful SSI hex wargame on a console built for FMV — the newsreel briefings are the only video, and critics still called it the deepest game on the system.
games.cheats: None known on 3DO (PC has scenario/prestige editors)
games.video: Brief windowed black-and-white archival footage and battle animations (can be disabled); FMV marginal
games.endings: Campaign branches by victory type (major/minor/loss) up to invasion of the US or defeat
games.trivia: GamePro praised the port's accuracy while disliking strategy games generally; Next Generation 4/5, EGM 7.125/10. A Jaguar version was never made.
games.variants: NA SSI release 1995; PAL Mindscape release 1995
games.notes: FMV content minimal; included as borderline. Extent of newsreel video on 3DO specifically: Unknown — verify.

games.title: Road Rash
games.source: Original production; 32-bit reboot of EA's Genesis Road Rash series
games.alsoOn: Sega CD (1995), PlayStation, Saturn, Windows (1996); Jaguar CD and M2 versions cancelled
games.cast: Riders played by crew and local AFM racers; Randy Breen (EA) as the motor cops; directed by Rod Gross
games.cidTrigger: A&M Records soundtrack: Soundgarden, Monster Magnet, Paw, Swervedriver, Therapy?, Hammerbox (menus/cutscenes); in-race score is original Don Veca music
games.hook: EA wrecked a rented Ducati filming 25 minutes of grunge-scored biker-gang video for the 3DO's best-selling game.
games.cheats: No codes listed. Hidden trick: brake to a stop, then press LS+RS and Up to get off the bike and walk around. (GameFAQs)
games.video: ~25 min of live-action FMV; roughly 2/3-screen window, ~15 fps Cinepak-style compression, heavy grain
games.difficulty: Moderate; five levels with rising opponent aggression and faster bikes
games.endings: Single ending after Level 5; win/lose/wipeout/busted cutscene variants between races
games.trivia: The yellow Yamaha FZR1000 in the videos was producer Randy Breen's own bike. The wrecked red Ducati from a botched stunt was later displayed in EA's corporate lobby.
games.variants: NA long box; EU big box; JP release via EA Victor; later Panasonic bundle listings in UK
games.notes: EGM Best Driving Game and Best 3DO Game of 1994. Only the Sega CD version plays the licensed songs during races.

games.title: The Need for Speed
games.alt: Road & Track Presents: The Need for Speed; Road & Track Presents: OverDrivin' (JP)
games.source: Original production in partnership with Road & Track magazine; 3DO is the original platform
games.alsoOn: DOS (Special Edition 1995), PlayStation, Saturn (1996), Windows SE (1996); Jaguar CD port cancelled
games.cast: Unnamed actor as the 'X-Man' rival; real supercars on camera
games.cidTrigger: Original music under car showcase videos; licensed car manufacturer footage unlikely to be claimed
games.hook: The franchise that became NFS began as a 3DO car-magazine showcase with live-action road videos of eight exotics.
games.cheats: Win the tournament to unlock Lost Vegas; a second win unlocks rally and mirrored modes. GameFAQs lists button and password codes only for the PlayStation and Saturn versions.
games.video: Short live-action car showcase clips and X-Man taunts; reduced window, ~15 fps, Cinepak-quality
games.difficulty: Moderate; police and traffic on three point-to-point tracks
games.endings: No story ending; tournament completion unlocks bonus content
games.trivia: Road & Track engineers helped tune vehicle handling and gear-lever audio. Development shared staff with Test Drive and was co-developed by Pioneer Productions.
games.variants: NA long box; JP 'OverDrivin'' with Nissan-sponsored spin-offs on later platforms; Special Edition only on PC
games.notes: JP 3DO release c. Dec 9 1994 per citation. Next Generation gave the 3DO version just 2/5.

games.title: Crash 'n Burn
games.publisher: Crystal Dynamics (NA), Panasonic / Crystal Dynamics (JP) — verify
games.cast: Unnamed actors as the six drivers: Fang, Druger, Tasman Twix, Max Amillion, Klaw, Rocker
games.hook: The only game on shelves the day 3DO launched, padded with hammy live-action death threats from costumed drivers.
games.video: Short live-action driver intro/taunt clips in a reduced window; ~15 fps, grainy early 3DO codec
games.difficulty: Moderate to hard; no multiplayer, long tournament grind
games.endings: Single ending on winning the tournament
games.trivia: Pack-in for the original Panasonic FZ-1 and the system's sole launch-day title. Mark Cerny is credited as designer; the game is set in 2044.
games.variants: Pack-in disc with FZ-1; separate retail long box; JP release Mar 26 1994
games.notes: GameFan 1993 Megaward Best Driving Game (3DO). Actor names not documented on Wikipedia/Giant Bomb.

games.title: Total Eclipse
games.publisher: Crystal Dynamics (NA/EU), Crystal Dynamics / Panasonic (JP) — verify
games.alsoOn: PlayStation as Total Eclipse Turbo (1995, US launch window)
games.hook: Crystal Dynamics' Star Fox-style shooter bookended by SGI-rendered CG, later shoved out as a PS1 launch title.
games.cheats: Stage select: in Options highlight Quit/Previews, hold X and press B, L, A, release X and press B, L, A, B, L, A. Free Flight Zone: pause, enter Options, highlight Resume and press B, A, C, A, B, A, LS, LS+RS, X, X (a skull confirms), then LS, A, B, LS, A, B, X, X, X. (GameFAQs)
games.video: Brief pre-rendered CG intro/ending; full-ish window, ~15 fps
games.difficulty: Hard; sensitive controls, punishing hit detection, limited continues
games.trivia: Bundled with Panasonic's FZ-1 in some 1994 UK promotions and later paired with Gex in a Panasonic coupon offer. Sequel Solar Eclipse went to Saturn/PS1.
games.variants: NA long box; EU release Sep 1994; JP Mar 26 1994; Turbo on PS1
games.notes: FMV limited to short CG cinematics; practically a conventional shooter.

games.title: Off-World Interceptor
games.alsoOn: Saturn and PlayStation as Off-World Interceptor Extreme (1995)
games.cast: Unnamed comedy actors as MST3K-style commentators
games.hook: A bounty-hunting monster-truck shooter heckled between levels by a pair of live-action Mystery Science Theater-style goofballs.
games.cheats: $9,999,900: on the Options screen select Sound, then press A, B, C six times and L. (GameFAQs)
games.video: Live-action comedy skits in a reduced window; ~15 fps
games.difficulty: Hard early on; reviewers noted initial frustration
games.trivia: 3DO Magazine gave it 5/5 while AllGame gave 2.5/5. The Extreme ports were re-tuned to feel like the original's arcade mode.
games.variants: NA/EU long box; Extreme editions on Saturn/PS1
games.notes: JP release not found — verify. Two-player split-screen deathmatch Battle mode.

games.title: The Horde
games.alsoOn: DOS (1994, bundled with RealMagic MPEG card), FM Towns (1995), Saturn (1996)
games.cast: Kirk Cameron (Chauncey), Michael Gregory (Kronus Maelor)
games.hook: Kirk Cameron defends villages from cow-eating Hordlings in a game whose first pressing wiped your other 3DO saves.
games.video: Live-action cutscenes shot over two days; reduced window, ~15 fps; some versions cut video to slideshows
games.difficulty: Moderate; escalating seasons with taxes and tougher Hordlings
games.endings: Single ending after the final region
games.trivia: Jim Carrey and Michael Richards were considered for Chauncey. A chocolate prop key nearly killed the chocolate-allergic actor playing the Chancellor; it was reshot with carob.
games.variants: NA long box with a Hordling mouth that opens; recalled first pressing replaced with save-prompt discs; JP Jul 23 1994
games.notes: CGW 1994 Best On-Screen Performance (Michael Gregory) and Best Musical Score.

games.title: Shock Wave
games.alt: Shock Wave: Invasion Earth 2019; ショックウェーブ (JP)
games.alsoOn: Pippin; later bundled with Jumpgate as Shockwave Assault on PS1, Saturn, Windows, Mac (1996)
games.cast: Unnamed actors as Cmdr. Crane, Maj. Alaina Stewart, Dr. Lawrence — verify
games.hook: EA's texture-mapped alien-invasion shooter with live actors barking orders at you mid-mission through a cockpit video feed.
games.cheats: Pause (P), press B, A, C, C, A, A, then Stop to unpause; pause again and enter A, B, A, C, A, A, B, A, X for invincibility, C, A, A, B, A, X for super lasers, or A, C, A, B, A, A, C, A, A, A, X for smart bombs. Leave the end screen after the credits to play a hidden Mission 11. (GameFAQs)
games.video: Live-action and CG cutscenes plus in-HUD video messages; reduced window, ~15 fps; EGM called the FMV 'sharp'
games.difficulty: Moderate; over-sensitive controls, 10 missions each ending in a boss
games.endings: Single ending; save file carries into Operation Jumpgate
games.trivia: Pack-in for the Goldstar 3DO and Creative's 3DO Blaster PC card. The F-177 fighter is modeled on the F-117 Nighthawk and auto-hovers so it cannot crash.
games.variants: NA long box; Goldstar pack-in; JP EA Victor release; 3DO version has 10 missions vs 15 in later ports
games.notes: Actor names not documented in Wikipedia/Giant Bomb/MobyGames — verify via credits.

games.title: Shock Wave 2: Beyond the Gate
games.alt: ショックウェーブ2 (JP) — verify
games.publisher: Electronic Arts (NA/EU); EA Victor (JP) — verify; rights later sold to Aztech New Media
games.source: Original production; sequel to Shock Wave
games.alsoOn: Mac (ported 1996, shelved; released 1998 in Mac Pack Blitz compilation)
games.cast: Unnamed actors as space-pirate mercenaries in Hawaiian shirts; CG aliens/robots
games.hook: A two-disc 3DO sequel with Hawaiian-shirted mercs and unconvincing CG aliens that EA barely bothered to port anywhere else.
games.cheats: Fire a laser and pause while it's visible: A, A, A, C, R, Stop = invincibility; R, R, B, A, B, R, A, C, A, Stop, then pause again and A, C, A, R, A, A, B, A, A, A, Stop = end the mission successfully. (GameFAQs)
games.video: Live-action intro and briefing videos mixed with CG; reduced window, ~15 fps
games.difficulty: Moderate to hard; frame rate drops in busy fights
games.trivia: A finished Mac port sat unreleased for two years because 3DO sales were too low to justify it.
games.variants: NA long box (2 discs); EU release 1995; JP release — verify
games.notes: Wikipedia coverage thin; disc count from retail listings and Video Game Critic.

games.title: Shockwave: Operation Jumpgate
games.source: Original production; add-on to Shock Wave
games.alsoOn: Bundled in Shockwave Assault on PS1, Saturn, Windows, Mac, Pippin (1996)
games.cast: Returning Shock Wave actors (Wildcard, Stewart, ICE); some footage reused — verify
games.hook: A rare console expansion disc that refuses to boot unless a Shock Wave save file is sitting in your 3DO's memory.
games.video: Short live-action/CG briefings; reduced window, ~15 fps
games.difficulty: Hard; Next Generation called it 'twice as challenging' as the original
games.endings: Single epilogue ending across five missions
games.trivia: Released May 19, 1995 as a standalone-priced disc but requires the original's save data to play.
games.variants: NA long box; EU 1995; later only as part of Shockwave Assault
games.notes: No JP release found. Five epilogue missions only.

games.title: Jurassic Park Interactive
games.publisher: Universal Interactive Studios (NA May 10, 1994; PAL 1994 per Wikipedia)
games.source: Film license (Jurassic Park, 1993); uses film footage and score
games.cast: Film footage with actors' faces cut out; unnamed look-alike actors in later scenes
games.cidTrigger: John Williams' Jurassic Park score and Universal film footage used in intro and cutscenes
games.hook: Universal's first game used real Jurassic Park footage, then hid every actor's face and hired look-alikes.
games.video: Film clips and look-alike footage in a reduced window, ~15 fps, heavy compression
games.difficulty: Normal/Hard/Expert settings alter guests to rescue and time limit
games.endings: Single ending once all guests reach the helipad and help is summoned
games.trivia: Originally planned as the 3DO's October 1993 pack-in but slipped to May 1994. About 10 people over 14 months on a $1–2M budget.
games.variants: NA long box; PAL release 1994; JP release (Famitsu reviewed)
games.notes: Only Jurassic Park game to use the film's footage and music. Kotaku ranked it among the worst JP games.

games.title: VR Stalker
games.source: Original production; published by the Mad Dog McCree company
games.cast: Unnamed actors in mission briefings — verify
games.hook: American Laser Games' lone non-shooting-gallery 3DO release: a cheesy flight sim from the studio founder who later built The Void.
games.cheats: Cheat mode: highlight Objective Menu and press LS, A, C, A, C, B, B, B (a creature picture appears), then C, LS, RS, C, RS, X, LS, A = god mode, B, B, B, LS, C, A, C, LS = 99,000 missiles, A, A, C, B, RS, LS, B, A = X2 superplane. Level passwords listed, e.g. Arizona 5KK-LQG-77K. (GameFAQs)
games.video: Live-action briefing cutscenes; small window, ~15 fps — verify extent
games.difficulty: Fast and varied but shallow; mixed reviews (EGM 24/40)
games.trivia: Billed as the first flight sim on 3DO. The PAL version was reworked in gameplay and graphics and resubmitted to The 3DO Company for approval.
games.variants: NA long box (ALG 1994); PAL BMG release 1995 with revised gameplay
games.notes: FMV content not well documented online; confirm live-action briefings from footage before scheduling.

games.title: Mazer
games.source: Original production; also released as an arcade cabinet (1995)
games.cast: Digitized actors as the four playable soldiers (unnamed)
games.hook: The Mad Dog McCree studio tried a Smash TV-style shooter with digitized actors and got 1/5 from Next Generation.
games.video: Pre-rendered CG intro and digitized-actor sprites; minimal streamed video — verify
games.difficulty: Hard and repetitive; poor hit feedback
games.trivia: Enemies are the 'Semag-Resal' — 'Laser Games' spelled backwards. One of ALG's last 3DO titles before it pivoted to children's software.
games.notes: EU/JP release unconfirmed (French Joystick review was likely an import). Streamed FMV content minimal — borderline inclusion.

games.title: Alone in the Dark
games.alt: アローン・イン・ザ・ダーク (JP)
games.developer: Krisalis Software (3DO port of Infogrames original)
games.publisher: Interplay / I•Motion (NA), Infogrames (EU) (Wikipedia); JP EA Victor per earlier research
games.alsoOn: DOS, Mac, PC-98, FM Towns, RISC OS, iOS (2014); Jaguar CD/32X ports cancelled
games.hook: The survival-horror progenitor reached consoles first on 3DO, with CD audio and voiced text from the PC CD edition.
games.video: Streamed video minimal: short rendered intro/ending; most cutscenes are engine polygons — verify
games.difficulty: Moderate; instant deaths and obtuse puzzles
games.trivia: Krisalis also handled the Archimedes port. EGM scored the 3DO version 9/8/7/8/8.
games.variants: NA Interplay long box; EU Infogrames; JP EA Victor release
games.notes: Likely minimal streamed FMV; included as a 'cutscenes only' edge case. Confirm 3DO-specific intro before use.

games.title: Alone in the Dark 2
games.alt: Alone in the Dark 2: Jack Is Back (EU); アローン・イン・ザ・ダーク 2 (JP)
games.developer: Krisalis Software (3DO port of Infogrames original)
games.publisher: Interplay Productions (NA 3DO), Infogrames (EU) (Wikipedia); JP EA Victor per earlier research
games.alsoOn: DOS, PC-98, FM Towns, Mac, Saturn, PlayStation
games.hook: A 'direct port of the PC title' that hit 3DO in late 1995 just as the Saturn/PS1 remakes with new FMV were arriving.
games.video: Minimal streamed video; cinematics are largely engine-rendered — verify
games.difficulty: Hard; combat-heavy with fixed camera angles
games.trivia: Maximum (2/5) complained the 3DO port used flat-shaded polygons, a smaller screen and a low frame rate, calling the game too old to convert.
games.variants: NA Interplay (Nov 22 1995); EU 'Jack Is Back'; JP EA Victor
games.notes: The Saturn/PS1 versions got the new FMV, not 3DO. Borderline inclusion.

games.title: Rise of the Robots
games.developer: Mirage Technologies, additional work by Instinct Design (Wikipedia); 3DO publisher Absolute Entertainment. Port studio not named in Wikipedia.
games.alsoOn: Amiga, CD32, DOS, SNES, Mega Drive, Game Gear, CD-i; arcade prototype
games.cast: Brian May (Queen) contributed the track 'The Dark'
games.cidTrigger: Brian May's 'The Dark' in the intro/title
games.hook: The most hyped and most hated fighter of 1994 landed on 3DO with its longest-ever pre-rendered cyborg cinematics.
games.cheats: Supervisor playable via code on some versions — 3DO unverified
games.video: Lengthy pre-rendered CG intro and character cinemas; near-full window, ~15 fps
games.difficulty: Frustrating; tiny move set, hard to even land basic punches
games.endings: Single ending; can only play as the Cyborg in story mode
games.trivia: Absolute kept the 3DO rights when it sold the others back to Mirage. EGM gave it 3.5/10 and called it 'by far the worst fighting game I've ever seen.'
games.variants: NA Absolute long box; EU release Mar 1995
games.notes: Reviewers singled out the overlong cinemas and load times on 3DO.

games.title: Sesame Street: Numbers
games.alt: A Visit to Sesame Street: Numbers
games.source: TV license (Sesame Street); DOS/CD-i original 1991–92 ported to 3DO
games.cast: Muppet performers in archival clips: Caroll Spinney, Frank Oz, Jim Henson, Kevin Clash, Jerry Nelson, Martin P. Robinson
games.cidTrigger: Sesame Workshop TV clips and songs (counting segments, Count von Count, etc.)
games.hook: Elmo leads toddlers through five locations stuffed with vintage 1970s–80s Sesame Street counting clips on a $700 console.
games.video: Archival TV clips (puppet and animated segments) in a reduced window, ~15 fps, VHS-quality source
games.trivia: Originally built for CD-i and DOS by Viridis in 1991–92; a Letters companion was also released. RetroAchievements has a set for it.
games.variants: NA EA Kids long box; companion title Sesame Street: Letters
games.notes: Video is the main attraction (TV clips and songs), so fmv rated 4 despite 'cutscenes' category. NA-only release.

games.title: Gex
games.source: Original production; 3DO is the original platform
games.alsoOn: PlayStation, Saturn (1995–96), Windows (1996), PSN (2009), Gex Trilogy (2025)
games.cast: Dana Gould (voice of Gex; wrote all his dialogue)
games.hook: The 3DO's million-selling mascot platformer, with Dana Gould one-liners and an 18-minute hidden staff-photo credits reel.
games.cheats: Hidden code opens a stage select with 80+ slots; a hidden shooter minigame (Evan Wells' Stanford project)
games.video: Short pre-rendered CG intro/outro; near-full window, ~15 fps; later ports cleaned up the cinemas
games.difficulty: Moderate; 28 levels, boss stages gate saves
games.endings: Standard ending plus hidden 18-min credits sequence for full completion
games.trivia: A designer whose level was cut hid messages in the game and was fired after playtesters found them. Development ran 21 months past a June 1994 target.
games.variants: NA long box; JP Apr 21 1995; UK BMG May 12 1995; later Panasonic console bundles
games.modern: Yes (Gex Trilogy, Limited Run 2025 — PS1-based, not the 3DO version; PSN 2009)
games.notes: 3DO is the only version with battery saves; others use passwords. Sales ~750k–1M.

games.title: Captain Quazar
games.hook: A square-jawed parody space hero built by two guys in a garage, with CG cinemas EGM called 'compelling' and 3DO's own money behind it.
games.cheats: Super power-up: pause (P) and press L, R, L, R, L, R, B. Teleporter codes per level open secret areas (e.g. level 1 BACACABA = Money Fort). Interrogating enemies reveals secret levels and items. (GameFAQs)
games.video: Pre-rendered CG intro and between-level cinemas; near-full window, ~15 fps
games.trivia: Cyclone's first project: founders Helmut Kobler and Ron Little prototyped it over six months in Palo Alto and East Oakland before 3DO funded it.
games.notes: JP release unconfirmed — verify. Saves allowed only at level start.

games.title: Immercenary
games.alt: Perfect (working title); パーフェクトワールド / Perfect World (JP)
games.source: Original production inspired by Neal Stephenson's Snow Crash
games.cast: Chris Stashuk (Chameleon; FMO co-founder); video production headed by Marla Johnson-Norris
games.hook: A Snow Crash-inspired cyberspace deathmatch RPG where you 'jack out' to live-action real-world scenes shot on video to save money.
games.video: Live-action video cutscenes in the 'real world' hub; reduced window, ~15 fps, shot on video not film
games.difficulty: Moderate to hard; level-based ranking climb through Perfect's citizens
games.trivia: Conceived in 1993 at EA producer Jim Simmons' request to showcase the 3DO; EA renamed it from 'Perfect' to Immercenary. Writer Elton Pruitt drew heavily on Snow Crash.
games.variants: NA long box (Mar 1995); EU release; JP EA Victor Sep 22 1995
games.notes: Often cited as a forgotten precursor to online-style deathmatch RPGs.

games.title: Burning Soldier
games.alt: バーニングソルジャー (JP, same title)
games.cast: Nigel Hogge (narration); Robbie Danzie (ending vocal 'Summer Leads the Way')
games.save: Unknown — verify (score save to NVRAM likely; infinite continues restart current mission)
games.peripherals: Standard 3DO control pad; 2 players simultaneous (debug mode allows 4)
games.hook: A 3DO rail shooter where the pre-rendered movie never loops — if the video ends before the boss dies, you lose, no matter your health.
games.cheats: Debug/hidden mode enabling 4-player play reported; stage select unverified
games.video: Near full-screen pre-rendered Cinepak-style CG streamed continuously, ~15 fps, sprites overlaid; praised as best 3DO FMV of 1994 by GameFan
games.difficulty: Easy-to-moderate; no extra lives but unlimited continues, boss timeouts can force game over
games.trivia: Both JP and Western releases are fully voiced in English with no subtitles; GameFan gave it Best FMV and Best Music (3DO) 1994, while Edge called it 'the most uninspiring 3DO release ever'.
games.variants: JP Pack-In-Video release; NA/EU Panasonic long-box; Polydor arranged-soundtrack album (JP, Sept 1994)
games.notes: Whole game is streamed pre-rendered video with sprite overlays (Rebel Assault model). FMV 9.

games.title: Theatre Wars: Goraku no Dendo
games.alt: シアターウォーズ 娯楽の殿堂 (Theatre Wars: Goraku no Dendou)
games.cast: Unknown — verify (Japanese stage performers/dancers)
games.cidTrigger: Music used in the staged show sequences
games.hook: Run a theatre in the year 2050, budget for sets, dancers and music, and watch your show play out as video — or go bankrupt and become a parking lot.
games.video: Windowed live-action show/performance clips, ~15 fps (verify)
games.difficulty: Opaque Japanese-only management; easy to go bankrupt
games.endings: Success/bankruptcy outcomes per stage; theatre demolished on failure
games.trivia: Published by advertising giant Hakuhodo (released May 14 1994); MobyGames tags it 'Full Motion Video'. Featured in Nerd & Tie's '3DOh No!' series as 'not very' good.
games.notes: Theatre-management sim set in 2050: you budget for sets, dancers and music, and a badly reviewed show bankrupts you (MobyGames, Giant Bomb). Released May 14, 1994 (JP). MobyGames tags it Full Motion Video, but how much of the show is streamed video is still unconfirmed, so fmv 5 is an estimate; the 3DOh No! let's play on YouTube shows it. PriceCharting has a page but no recorded sales.

games.title: Casper
games.alsoOn: PlayStation, Saturn (same game); different Casper games on SNES, Game Boy, 3DO is this version
games.cast: Malachi Pearson (Casper), Brad Garrett (Fatso), Joe Nipote (Stretch), Joe Alaskey (Stinkie) — reprising film voices
games.cidTrigger: Film-derived score cues and dialogue in cutscenes
games.hook: The very last 3DO game released in North America — a pre-rendered Casper puzzle adventure with the movie's actual ghost voices.
games.video: Short pre-rendered intro/act transitions (SGI/Alias renders); gameplay uses pre-rendered sprites, not streamed video
games.difficulty: Moderate; obscure puzzles and disorienting mansion layout per EGM
games.trivia: Graphics rendered on Silicon Graphics workstations with Alias; Next Generation praised the ghosts' true transparency. Widely cited as the 3DO's final NA release (Sept 1996).
games.variants: NA only on 3DO; PS/Saturn versions in NA/EU/JP
games.notes: Not an FMV game: streamed video limited to brief rendered cinematics (unverified). fmv 1.

games.title: Sailor Moon (Pretty Soldier Sailor Moon S, 3DO)
games.alsoOn: 3DO exclusive (other Sailor Moon S fighters on SNES/PS/Saturn are different games)
games.cast: Anime seiyuu reprising roles incl. Kotono Mitsuishi (Sailor Moon)
games.cidTrigger: Toei anime footage and licensed Sailor Moon theme music in the opening
games.hook: The only Sailor Moon fighter with the anime cast on 3DO — Naoko Takeuchi supervised it, and it still sold under 20,000 copies.
games.cheats: Easy mode for one-button specials; no codes widely known
games.video: Anime opening/ending clips streamed in a window, ~15 fps; in-game is 2D sprites with zooming camera
games.trivia: Nine playable Sailor Soldiers (no Saturn); Famitsu reported ~19,075 lifetime sales. Retro Gamer counts it among the 3DO's stronger 2D fighters.
games.notes: Anime FMV limited to opening/intermission clips (unverified extent); fmv 2.
games.criticSrc: average of 2 reviews on Wikipedia (NGen, Player One)

games.title: Scramble Cobra
games.cast: Unknown — verify (live-action briefing actors)
games.peripherals: Standard 3DO control pad; 3DO FlightStick support unverified
games.hook: Genki's follow-up to Burning Soldier swaps streamed movies for a polygon AH-1 Cobra — and live-action briefings reviewers found dull.
games.video: Live-action story/briefing clips in a window; gameplay is real-time polygon 3D from cockpit
games.trivia: Fictional war of empire R invading K; sold under 9,000 copies in Japan. Next Generation: 'not bad enough to be painful'.
games.notes: MobyGames notes live-action video tells the story; gameplay is not FMV. fmv 2.

games.title: Starblade
games.source: Arcade original (Namco Starblade, 1991, polygon arcade game)
games.alsoOn: Arcade, Sega CD, PlayStation (Starblade Alpha), Wii VC (JP), i-Mode, iOS/Android
games.hook: Namco's polygon arcade classic rebuilt as streamed pre-rendered video on 3DO — with a switch between flat-shaded and textured looks.
games.cheats: Graphics mode toggle (flat vs textured); none else known
games.video: Full-screen pre-rendered backgrounds streamed as Cinepak video with real-time polygon enemies/cursor overlaid; compression artifacts blur the starfield; bosses time out on a fixed clock
games.difficulty: Frustrating per GamePro: no power-ups, slow cursor
games.trivia: Because backgrounds are video, boss fights end at the same moment every time regardless of play (unlike the Sega CD port). Starblade Alpha on PS was criticized as nearly identical to the 3DO version.
games.modern: Yes (arcade version via Namco Museum/Tekken 5 minigame; 3DO version itself: No)
games.notes: Pre-rendered streamed backgrounds with polygon overlays; fmv 8.

games.title: Flashback: The Quest for Identity
games.alt: Flashback (JP: フラッシュバック)
games.publisher: U.S. Gold / Interplay (NA), Electronic Arts Victor (JP), U.S. Gold (EU)
games.alsoOn: Amiga, DOS, SNES, Genesis, Sega CD, CD-i, Jaguar, Mac, and later remasters
games.hook: The CD-era Flashback: Delphine's rotoscoped classic with its cutscenes redone as pre-rendered CG movies with voice acting.
games.cheats: Level passwords per difficulty. GameFAQs lists them for the CD-i, Genesis and Sega CD versions but none specific to 3DO.
games.video: Windowed pre-rendered CG cutscenes with voice, ~15 fps; gameplay is 2D sprites
games.endings: Single ending (Conrad escapes in suspended animation)
games.trivia: The 3DO port derives from the DOS CD-ROM re-release with re-rendered FMV cutscenes; Next Generation said the 3DO pad 'doesn't interfere (much)'.
games.variants: JP Feb 17 1995 (EA Victor), NA Mar 24 1995, EU 1995
games.modern: Yes (Flashback 25th Anniversary / remasters on Switch, PS4, Xbox, PC, GOG — not the 3DO build)
games.notes: FMV limited to rendered cutscenes; fmv 2.

games.title: Lost Files of Sherlock Holmes: The Case of the Serrated Scalpel
games.alt: The Lost Files of Sherlock Holmes
games.alsoOn: DOS (floppy and CD), later Windows via ScummVM
games.cast: David Ian Davies (Holmes), Laurie Main (Watson) — filmed clips and voices
games.peripherals: Standard 3DO control pad (3DO Mouse support unverified)
games.hook: The full-talkie Holmes: every painted portrait replaced with a live-action actor in a window, making a 1992 PC adventure feel like a 3DO interactive movie.
games.video: Small windowed live-action talking-head clips during all dialogue, ~10–15 fps; backgrounds remain 2D art
games.difficulty: Moderate; large inventory and many locations
games.endings: Single ending (Holmes solves the Serrated Scalpel murders)
games.trivia: The DOS version used speech only in the intro, St Pancras and ending scenes; the 3DO version voices everything and removes Watson's journal.
games.notes: Dialogue-driven game where live-action clips run throughout; fmv 4. MobyGames scores shown are the multi-platform entry totals.

games.title: Blue Forest Story
games.alt: Blue Forest Story: Kaze no Fūin / ブルーフォレスト物語 風の封印
games.hook: A late Japan-only 3DO RPG with a CGI opening, HP-costing spells and a notorious hot-spring scene.
games.video: CGI opening movie only; gameplay is 2D sprites with no voice acting
games.endings: Two protagonists (Wallace/Valerus and Rakjit); choices affect character views between chapters
games.trivia: Released April 26 1996 by Panasonic, among the last JP 3DO titles; soundtrack by Psy-fa the Field's Mechanique Valley.
games.variants: 3DO JP (Panasonic); PS JP (Right Stuff) with changed opening
games.notes: Streamed video is the opening movie only; fmv 1. Not listed on PriceCharting.

games.title: Sotsugyou Final
games.publisher: Shar Rock (JP); HOKUBU Communication also credited
games.alsoOn: PC-98, FM Towns, X68000, Mac, PC Engine CD, Saturn, PlayStation (Graduation R), WonderSwan (other editions)
games.cast: Unknown — verify (anime seiyuu for the five students)
games.cidTrigger: Vocal theme songs from the Graduation OVA/anime
games.hook: The 3DO 'Final' cut of the original girl-raising sim — teach five students to graduation, dressed up with anime movies and voices.
games.video: Anime-style opening/event movies in a window, ~15 fps (extent unverified)
games.difficulty: Stat-management; easy to fail individual students
games.endings: Multiple graduation endings depending on each student's development
games.trivia: Released Dec 9 1994 (Shar Rock); the 3DO also got Sotsugyou II: Neo Generation Special in 1995. The franchise spawned a 1995 OVA.
games.variants: JP only; demo disc also circulated
games.notes: Anime FMV presence inferred from the 'Final' edition's enhanced presentation — verify extent; fmv 2 estimate. Not listed on PriceCharting.

games.title: Yu Yu Hakusho (3DO)
games.alsoOn: 3DO exclusive (other YYH fighters on SNES/Genesis are different games)
games.cast: Anime seiyuu (verify); narrator between fights
games.peripherals: Standard 3DO control pad; 2 players, 5-on-5 team battle
games.cidTrigger: Actual Studio Pierrot anime episode clips and series music between fights
games.hook: A fighter built from digitized anime cels, with real episode clips stitched between bouts — Next Generation said 'avoid at all costs'.
games.video: Windowed anime clips from the TV series, ~15 fps; in-game sprites are digitized cels
games.difficulty: Low-to-moderate; only weak/strong attacks, slow projectiles
games.endings: Scenario Mode follows the Dark Tournament then Sensui arc to one ending
games.trivia: 15 characters; Hardcore Gaming 101 called it 'an interesting failure'. Released Dec 23 1994.
games.notes: Anime FMV between every story fight — a meaningful share of Scenario Mode; fmv 3.

games.title: Policenauts
games.genre: Point-and-click adventure / visual novel with light-gun segments
games.cast: Hideyuki Tanaka (Jonathan Ingram), Kyoko Terase (Meryl), Kikuko Inoue (Karen), Shōzō Iizuka (Ed Brown), Iemasa Kayumi (Tokugawa)
games.peripherals: Standard 3DO control pad; 3DO Mouse (verify); light gun only on Saturn
games.cidTrigger: Konami score and vocal end theme
games.hook: Kojima's Lethal Weapon-in-space: the 3DO cut is where the AIC cel-animated cutscenes first appeared, at 24 fps the PlayStation couldn't match.
games.cheats: None known; Pilot Disk demo includes glossary and design docs
games.video: Windowed cel-animated cutscenes (AIC) at 24 fps, Cinepak; most of the game is voiced stills
