games.source: Original production; scenario by Hideki Sonoda
games.alsoOn: PlayStation and Windows 95 (same day); DVD-PG port (Pioneer, 1998)
games.cast: Megumi Hayashibara (Maria Helsing; sings ending theme)
games.peripherals: Standard pad; Saturn internal memory / backup cart for saves
games.hook: A vampire detective with a time machine chases a missing doctor onto a 1939 zeppelin, opening with a 30-minute CG movie.
games.video: Lavish CG cutscenes; PS version's first disc is entirely demo/cutscenes; Saturn graphics judged slightly lower than PS
games.trivia: Famitsu scored Saturn 6/7/6/7 and found the only difference from PS was the PS version's sharper graphics; one reviewer said the lavishly animated cutscenes are worth watching at least once.
games.notes: Released 26 Jul 1996 on Saturn, PS and Windows 95 (Wikipedia en/ja). Not live-action. Sequel Jikuu Tantei DD 2 (PS, 1998) not checked for Saturn.
games.criticSrc: average of 3 reviews on Wikipedia and Japanese Wikipedia (Famitsu, Sega Saturn Magazine JP, Saturn Fan)

games.title: Shinseiki Evangelion
games.alt: 新世紀エヴァンゲリオン / Neon Genesis Evangelion
games.source: Gainax/Tatsunoko TV anime Neon Genesis Evangelion (1995)
games.cast: TV series voice cast (Megumi Ogata, Megumi Hayashibara, Yuko Miyamura and others)
games.cidTrigger: Evangelion music and voice cast; animation is new (Tatsunoko), not lifted from the series
games.hook: The only Eva game released while the show was airing: an interactive anime where you choose Shinji's actions between movies and fight Angels with quick-time inputs.
games.video: Newly animated cel movies (Tatsunoko Production, script Hiroshi Yamaguchi) with full TV voice cast; battles are 'command visual battles' with timed inputs over animation
games.endings: Multiple; three routes (wandering, school, battle) and bad endings
games.trivia: Set between episodes 9 and 10; amnesiac Shinji can form the 'Earth Defense Band' with Hikari singing the original song 'Kiseki no Senshi Evangelion'. An original Angel was designed by Ikuto Yamashita.
games.variants: Original (1 Mar 1996); budget reprint with new package (14 Feb 1997)
games.notes: Japanese Wikipedia: an interactive movie of animation with choices between movies, plus a replay mode to watch your playthrough as continuous animation. Sega Saturn Magazine scored it 22/30. Disc count unconfirmed (1 or 2).

games.title: Shinseiki Evangelion: 2nd Impression
games.alt: 新世紀エヴァンゲリオン 2nd Impression / Neon Genesis Evangelion: Second Impression
games.source: Original side story to the Evangelion TV anime (new pilot Mayumi Yamagishi)
games.cast: TV series voice cast (Megumi Ogata, Yuko Miyamura, Megumi Hayashibara and others); Kyoko Hikami (Mayumi Yamagishi)
games.cidTrigger: Evangelion music and voice cast; animation is new (Ashi Productions)
games.hook: Sega's second Eva game adds new pilot-classmate Mayumi Yamagishi, Ashi Productions animation and fully polygonal Eva battles.
games.video: New anime movies by Ashi Productions (director Yasushi Murayama, script Hiroshi Yamaguchi); battles are polygon with weapon movies; scenario replay mode
games.endings: Multiple; four main routes (Mayumi, Asuka, Rei, Earth Defense Band)
games.trivia: Set between episodes 15 and 16. Mayumi Yamagishi was created for this game; first prints came with a single CD of the two original insert songs and three Carddass Masters cards.
games.variants: Standard JP release with single CD and cards
games.notes: Japanese Wikipedia: sequel released about a year after the first, alongside the first game's budget reprint (14 Feb 1997); exact date not confirmed. Like the first game it is told through animated movies, so fmv raised from 2 to 6.

games.title: Shinseiki Evangelion: Koutetsu no Girlfriend
games.alt: 新世紀エヴァンゲリオン 鋼鉄のガールフレンド / Neon Genesis Evangelion: Girlfriend of Steel
games.source: Original Gainax story set in the Evangelion TV continuity
games.alsoOn: Windows (1997), Macintosh, PlayStation (1998); Special Edition PS2/Windows (2006), PSP (2009)
games.cast: Megumi Hayashibara (Mana Kirishima), Hiro Yuuki (Musashi), TV series voice cast
games.cidTrigger: Evangelion music; new animation from Gainax
games.hook: Gainax's own Eva story, with new animation: transfer student Mana Kirishima falls for Shinji, and Asuka suspects she is a spy.
games.video: Newly produced anime (director Tatsuo Hashimoto, animation director Teishi Hiramatsu); window size verify
games.endings: Three endings (Mana, Asuka, Kaji); a fourth was added in the Special Edition
games.trivia: Won the 1997 Animation Kobe award for interactive software. A Mac version was made after fans collected signatures. Ending song 'Yokan' by Yoko Takahashi.
games.variants: Saturn release 1998; PS port 1998; Special Edition (PS2/PC 2006, PSP 2009) adds scenes
games.notes: Saturn and PS versions came out in 1998, after the 1997 Windows original (Japanese Wikipedia). Interactivity is mostly walking between plot events. Saturn publisher and disc count unconfirmed.

games.title: Macross: Do You Remember Love?
games.alt: 超時空要塞マクロス 愛・おぼえていますか / Chō Jikū Yōsai Macross: Ai Oboete Imasu ka
games.source: 1984 anime film Macross: Do You Remember Love?
games.cast: Film voice cast incl. Mari Iijima (Lynn Minmay); archive recordings of Arihiro Hase (Hikaru) in the intro
games.cidTrigger: Footage from the 1984 film and its songs ('Ai Oboete Imasu ka' by Mari Iijima)
games.hook: A shooter that walks you through the whole Macross movie, with the film's footage streamed between stages.
games.video: Footage from the 1984 film plus all-new animated sequences, incl. a new opening supervised by Shoji Kawamori
games.trivia: Released for Macross's 15th anniversary. The new opening, covering the war's start (TV episodes 1–3), was later included on Macross DVD/BD sets. Gameplay system inherited from Bandai's Saturn Gundam.
games.notes: Wikipedia: 2 discs, film footage plus new animation. Next Generation gave the Saturn version 2/5. Publisher Bandai Visual per the Japanese Wikipedia Saturn Gundam article; developer not confirmed. fmv 5: long film sequences between conventional shooter stages. No Saturn PriceCharting page found.

games.title: Policenauts
games.cast: Hideyuki Tanaka (Jonathan Ingram), Kikuko Inoue (Karen Hojo), Chiyoko Kawashima (Lorraine), Shozo Iizuka (Ed Brown), Yumi Touma (Ana Brown)
games.peripherals: Saturn pad; light gun (Virtua Gun) supported; Shuttle Mouse (verify)
games.cidTrigger: Original Konami music; low risk
games.hook: Hideo Kojima's anime cyberpunk adventure between Snatcher and Metal Gear Solid, with streamed anime cutscenes.
games.video: Cel-animated FMV by Anime International Company at the 3DO's 24 fps, no Cinepak; investigation screens are stills from the movies
games.trivia: Kojima insisted the Saturn port keep 24 fps video. A Konami of America English Saturn release was announced in 1996 and cancelled; a fan translation of the Saturn version came out in 2016.
games.variants: Slipcase with hardbound art book; adds scenes, restores PS cuts, includes making-of videos and a Kikuko Inoue interview
games.notes: Saturn release 13 Sep 1996, the last port (Wikipedia). Play moves seamlessly between cutscenes and stills from them, so fmv raised to 5. Disc count unconfirmed.
games.criticSrc: average of 2 reviews on Wikipedia (Famitsu, Sega Saturn Magazine JP)

games.title: 3x3 Eyes: Kyuusei Koushu
games.source: Yuzo Takada manga 3×3 Eyes and its OVA
games.alsoOn: Windows 95, PlayStation; collected in 3×3 Eyes Memorial DVD box (2002)
games.cidTrigger: Licensed anime material
games.hook: A 3×3 Eyes adventure with original anime scenes.
games.video: Streamed anime cutscenes (verify)
games.notes: en Wikipedia: Nihon Create game first on Windows 95 and PlayStation, then ported to Saturn as 'Kyuusei Koushu S'. Saturn release date, publisher, disc count and amount of streamed anime unconfirmed; year left blank because the Saturn port followed the PS release.

games.title: Kidou Senshi Gundam
games.alt: 機動戦士ガンダム / Mobile Suit Gundam
games.source: Mobile Suit Gundam (1979 TV anime / films)
games.cast: Original anime voice cast in reused footage (verify)
games.cidTrigger: Footage and music from the Gundam anime
games.hook: Bandai's first Gundam on Sega hardware replays the One Year War in 12 stages, with famous scenes newly reanimated by Sunrise.
games.video: New animation of classic scenes made by Sunrise for the game, plus voiced cut-ins at boss fights
games.difficulty: Moderate; Hard mode adds a Zeong Head fight
games.endings: Linear; first clear shows new anime stills, later clears a CG mobile suit gallery
games.trivia: Released 22 Nov 1995. The new animation was later included on a Gundam film LD box and reused in the PS2 Mobile Suit Gundam.
games.notes: Japanese Wikipedia: side-scroller where enemies also attack from the foreground and background; scenario follows the films with TV elements. fmv 3 for the new Sunrise animation between stages.

games.title: Virus
games.source: Original game; adapted into the anime Virus Buster Serge (1997)
games.cidTrigger: Original anime music
games.hook: Hudson's cyberpunk Saturn adventure with anime cutscenes, the seed of the Virus Buster Serge anime.
games.video: Mix of anime-style animation and CG (amount streamed unconfirmed)
games.notes: en Wikipedia: Hudson Soft developed and published it for Saturn; Next Generation gave it 2/5. Reviews in Game.EXE and Computer Gaming World suggest a PC version (verify). Disc count and amount of video unconfirmed.

games.title: Lunar: Silver Star Story
games.alt: ルナ シルバースターストーリー
games.source: Remake of Lunar: The Silver Star (Mega CD, 1992)
games.alsoOn: PlayStation (Lunar: Silver Star Story Complete, 1998; NA 1999 by Working Designs), Windows
games.peripherals: Standard pad; MPEG-ban edition (1997) uses the Video CD Card
games.cidTrigger: Original songs and anime
games.hook: The first Lunar remake, with new anime cutscenes; the MPEG-ban edition plays them through the Saturn's Video CD Card.
games.video: Fully animated anime cutscenes; MPEG-ban edition uses the Video CD Card for enhanced video
games.trivia: The 1997 'MPEG-ban' re-release is one of the few Saturn games using the Video CD Card. Working Designs planned an English Saturn 'Director's Cut' that became the 1999 PS release.
games.variants: Standard (4 Jul 1996); MPEG-ban (4 Jul 1997, Video CD Card)
games.notes: Saturn release 4 Jul 1996 by Kadokawa Shoten (Wikipedia). fmv 2: a long RPG with anime cutscenes.

games.title: Command & Conquer
games.alt: Command & Conquer: Tiberian Dawn (later retronym); コマンド&コンカー (JP)
games.publisher: Virgin Interactive (NA/EU); Japanese Saturn release publisher — verify
games.alsoOn: DOS, Windows, Mac, PlayStation, Nintendo 64 (no FMV); remastered on PC 2020
games.cast: Joseph D. Kucan (Kane), Eric Alan Martin and Westwood staff
games.peripherals: Sega Shuttle Mouse supported (verify); standard pad
games.cidTrigger: Frank Klepacki's original score is owned by EA and has turned up in Content ID via the Remastered soundtrack (verify)
games.hook: Kane's live-action sermons on a Saturn pad: the PC RTS that defined the genre squeezed onto Sega's 32-bit box, briefings and all.
games.video: Mission briefings and CG cinematics streamed in a reduced window with visible compression; exact window size and frame rate — verify
games.difficulty: Hard on a pad; late Nod and GDI missions are punishing without a mouse
games.endings: Separate GDI and Nod endings (one per disc); Nod has multiple short ending videos chosen by the player in the PC original — verify on Saturn
games.trivia: Kane was played by Joe Kucan, Westwood's own video director. Apart from Las Vegas actor Eric Alan Martin, the live-action cast were Westwood employees.
games.variants: GDI disc and Nod disc in one double jewel/Saturn case; PAL and JP versions
games.modern: Yes (C&C Remastered Collection, PC 2020; PC original released as freeware in 2007)
games.notes: Wikipedia: the Saturn and PS ports lack multiplayer, and only the PS port added the Covert Operations missions, so the Saturn version has the base campaigns only. Japanese Saturn release and publisher not confirmed by the sources (verify).

games.title: Crusader: No Remorse
games.developer: Origin Systems (console versions rewritten by Realtime Associates)
games.alsoOn: DOS, PlayStation; PC re-release on GOG
games.cast: Live-action cast in rebel-base and WEC cutscenes (names not confirmed)
games.hook: A faceless red-armoured Silencer, exploding office workers and B-movie live-action rebels: Origin's cult shooter on Saturn.
games.video: Live-action mission briefings and cutscenes in a letterboxed window with heavy compression — verify size and frame rate
games.difficulty: Hard; tight resources and instant-death traps
games.trivia: The console ports were rewritten from scratch at 320x240 and added new music; the Saturn's second CPU handles background calculations. Producer Jorg Newman called it 'a very conservative, very direct port'.
games.notes: Saturn port released 1997 alongside the PS version; it adds the forward roll from No Regret. Critics found the console controls over-complicated and animation jerky. Port studio credit unconfirmed.

games.title: Shinobi Legions
games.alt: Shinobi X (EU); Shin Shinobi Den (真・忍伝) (JP, verify)
games.cast: Live-action actors as Sho, Kazuma and Aya — names verify
games.hook: Shinobi gone full live-action ninja movie: costumed actors, digitised sprites and cheesy martial-arts cutscenes between stages.
games.video: Grainy live-action cutscenes in a windowed frame between stages — verify size and frame rate
games.difficulty: Moderate to hard; late stages are tough
games.trivia: The only names in the in-game credits are the live-action FMV crew, so the game's developers are unknown. Sega Europe had Richard Jacques replace the in-game music for Shinobi X; the cutscene music was kept.
games.variants: Shinobi X (EU, new music), Shinobi Legions (NA, Vic Tokai); JP release
games.notes: Europe got Shinobi X with a new Richard Jacques score; NA (Vic Tokai) kept the Japanese score. Critics split on the FMV cutscenes. Japanese title from memory (verify).
games.criticSrc: average of 6 reviews on Wikipedia (EGM, EPD, Fam, Maximum, NGen, Sega Saturn Magazine)

games.title: Solar Eclipse
games.publisher: Crystal Dynamics (NA); BMG Victor (JP); Tec Toy (Brazil)
games.cast: Claudia Christian
games.hook: Babylon 5's Claudia Christian barks orders in live-action briefings between Crystal Dynamics' fast space-shooter missions.
games.video: Live-action briefing video in a window; quality and frame rate — verify
games.trivia: Developed in 16 months under the title Titan; US marketing renamed it as a sequel to Total Eclipse, but Japan and Europe kept Titan Wars.
games.variants: Solar Eclipse (NA); Titan Wars (JP and EU)
games.notes: Wikipedia: released first on Saturn in NA, Europe and Japan. EGM's four reviewers averaged 7.75/10. Christian's role name not confirmed.

games.title: Off-World Interceptor Extreme
games.cast: Live-action commentators (names not confirmed)
games.hook: Monster-truck combat on alien planets with goofy live-action interludes in Crystal Dynamics' mid-90s house style.
games.video: Cutscenes with Mystery Science Theater 3000-style live-action commentators — window size verify
games.trivia: The Extreme version is tuned to feel like the 3DO original's arcade mode and adds a Training mode.
games.notes: GamePro's Saturn review praised the commentators in the cutscenes; Sega Saturn Magazine found the gameplay poor. EU publisher unconfirmed.

games.title: Street Fighter: The Movie
games.alt: Street Fighter: Real Battle on Film (JP, ストリートファイター リアルバトル オン フィルム)
games.alsoOn: PlayStation; separate arcade game by Incredible Technologies
games.cast: Jean-Claude Van Damme, Ming-Na Wen, Byron Mann, Kylie Minogue, Damian Chapa, Miguel A. Núñez Jr.; Darko Tuscan as Bison
games.cidTrigger: Film-based FMV and the Chage & Aska 'Something There' music video after Movie Battle; digitised likenesses of the film's cast
games.hook: Digitised Van Damme, Kylie and the rest of the film's cast in a Super Turbo-engine fighter, with FMV between Movie Battle bouts.
games.video: FMV cinemas in Movie Battle mode and a closing music video of Chage & Aska's 'Something There' — window size verify
games.endings: Movie Battle ends with a music video; Street Battle has per-character endings (verify)
games.trivia: Raúl Juliá was too ill to take part and died in October 1994; his film stunt double Darko Tuscan played Bison instead. The home game is not a port of the arcade release.
games.variants: Japanese release retitled Real Battle on Film
games.notes: JP Saturn release 11 August 1995 (a day before PS). EGM praised the FMV cinemas; Sega Saturn Magazine and GamePro panned the Saturn version for slowdown.
games.criticSrc: average of 8 reviews on Wikipedia (Allgame, EGM, Electric Playground, GameFan, Hyper, Maximum, NGen, Sega Saturn Magazine)

games.title: Road Rash
games.developer: Electronic Arts (Saturn version by Buzz Puppet Productions)
games.cast: Soundgarden, Monster Magnet, Paw, Therapy?, Swervedriver, Hammerbox (music videos) — verify Saturn lineup
games.cidTrigger: Licensed A&M Records soundtrack (Soundgarden 'Outshined'/'Rusty Cage' etc.) and full music videos on the disc
games.hook: Clubbing bikers to grunge: the 3DO classic's Soundgarden soundtrack and live-action race-end clips on Saturn.
games.video: About 25 minutes of live-action FMV from the 3DO original (race-end clips and music videos); windowed, compressed — verify size
games.endings: Live-action clips vary with result; one final ending
games.trivia: The 3DO original's live-action vignettes and A&M soundtrack carried over to the 32-bit ports.
games.notes: Saturn port 1996; reviewers found it no better than the 3DO/PS versions, and Mean Machines Sega called the FMV 'extremely annoying'. Mute or skip the music when recording.
games.criticSrc: average of 4 reviews on Wikipedia (Allgame, GamePro, Mean Machines Sega, Sega Saturn Magazine)

games.title: The Need for Speed
games.source: Port of The Need for Speed (3DO, 1994)
games.peripherals: Standard pad; Arcade Racer wheel support — verify
games.cidTrigger: Road & Track-licensed car showcase videos (verify)
games.hook: Road & Track's car showcase videos and a Lamborghini Diablo on a Saturn: the first Need for Speed, FMV intros and all.
games.video: Short music-backed showcase video for each car plus intro — window size verify
games.trivia: The series began as a collaboration with Road & Track, which supplied car data. The Saturn and PS versions add three tracks over the 3DO original.
games.notes: Japan got a Nissan-only spin-off, Over Drivin' GT-R (Saturn, 1996), not this game. GamePro rated the Saturn version comparable to the PS one.

games.title: Congo the Movie: The Lost City of Zinj
games.cast: Steven Anthony Jones (Butembo Kabalo)
games.hook: A forgotten Saturn Doom-style tie-in to the killer-gorilla movie, told through new live-action video with an original side story.
games.video: Original live-action FMV by A Commotion Pictures in TrueMotion S; no film clips — window size verify
games.trivia: The FMV was shot for the game (a side story about the sole survivor of the first TraviCom expedition) and the score is original, with nothing from the film soundtrack.
games.notes: Wikipedia confirms original FMV, not film clips, and an original score. Critics called it a dull Doom clone with cartoonish enemies.

games.title: Independence Day
games.publisher: Fox Interactive (NA, distributed by 20th Century Fox Home Entertainment); EA distributed internationally
games.cast: Film clips — cast names verify
games.peripherals: Standard pad; Saturn Link Cable (two consoles)
games.cidTrigger: Clips from the 20th Century Fox film between missions (verify) and David Arnold's score
games.hook: Shoot down city destroyers in the 1996 blockbuster's tie-in, with film clips between missions.
games.video: Film clips in a window — verify
games.trivia: Moved up to November 1996 to match the film's VHS release, then slipped to February 1997. The PS and Saturn versions were developed together.
games.notes: Wikipedia does not mention film clips; whether the Saturn disc has film footage or only FMV briefings is still unconfirmed (verify). Two-player split screen or Saturn Link Cable. Reviews mixed to negative.

games.title: Ghen War
games.cast: Live-action crew: Jenners, Gina, Akira, Boxhead (actors not named)
games.hook: A Saturn-exclusive mech shooter with live-action alien-war briefings from Sega's early Western push.
games.video: Story told through cutscenes done mostly in full-motion video — window size verify
games.endings: Multiple endings; the best has the crew hailed as heroes
games.trivia: Early deformable terrain: firing into a mountain wears it away. Saturn Power ranked it 99th in its 1998 Top 100 Saturn games.
games.variants: NA and PAL; JP release 26 April 1996
games.notes: Saturn exclusive by Jumpin' Jack Software. Critics were split on visuals and controls.
games.criticSrc: average of 5 reviews on Wikipedia (Allgame, EGM, Fam, NGen, Sega Saturn Magazine)

games.title: Minnesota Fats: Pool Legend
games.alt: Side Pocket 2: Densetsu no Hustler (サイドポケット2 伝説のハスラー) (JP)
games.source: Original production; sequel to Data East's Side Pocket. A different game shares the name on Genesis
games.alsoOn: Genesis (a different game with the same title and CG cutscenes)
games.cast: Live-action cast unnamed; some opponents played by Data East marketing staff. JP dub: Chikao Otsuka voices Fats
games.hook: You play as Minnesota Fats himself, hustling across America through live-action cutscenes shot on no budget, with Data East's marketing staff as the rival hustlers.
games.video: Small-window live-action FMV cutscenes between story-mode matches plus a short documentary on Fats; window size and frame rate not confirmed (verify)
games.difficulty: Moderate; aiming controls were criticised as clumsy
games.endings: Linear story mode through a run of US cities; one ending (verify)
games.trivia: Unlike the Genesis version, on Saturn you play as Fats rather than a rookie chasing him. The disc adds a training mode and a short documentary on Fats. Famitsu scored it 28/40.
games.variants: NA (Data East) and JP (Side Pocket 2: Densetsu no Hustler, 31 March 1995). No PAL release found
games.notes: FMV cutscenes and documentary confirmed. The JP Side Pocket 2 has the same story (Fats hunts his pupil Junior and Big G) with a Japanese voice cast. Next Generation gave the Saturn version 1/5.

games.title: Resident Evil
games.alsoOn: PlayStation (incl. Director's Cut), Windows, Nintendo DS (Deadly Silence); GameCube/modern remake is a separate game
games.cast: Charlie Kraslavsky (Chris), Inez Jesionowski (Jill), Greg Smith (Barry), Eric Pirius (Wesker), Jason Durkee (Joseph)
games.length: 5–8 hr first run; under 3 hr once learned
games.hook: The Saturn Resident Evil adds a Battle Game, new monsters and a second Tyrant fight, and it keeps the famously stilted live-action intro.
games.cheats: Battle Game mode unlocks when you finish the game; a button code to unlock it early has been reported (verify inputs)
games.video: Live-action FMV intro and endings (shot in Japan, on the Tama River bank and a Tokyo studio) plus short CG clips; the colour intro is a PC feature, consoles show it in black and white (verify Saturn)
games.difficulty: Moderate; Chris is harder (fewer item slots, no lockpick)
games.endings: Multiple endings per character depending on who survives (several per character)
games.trivia: The Saturn version adds a Battle Game mode, extra enemies and a second Tyrant fight. Capcom unveiled the Saturn port at the April 1997 Tokyo Game Show after hesitating over the hardware.
games.variants: JP Biohazard; NA and PAL Resident Evil. JP Satakore budget reprint (verify)
games.modern: No (Saturn version); the PS Director's Cut was sold on PSN
games.notes: Saturn port developer and EU publisher unconfirmed (verify). The FMV is Capcom's own footage, so Content ID risk is low.

games.title: Sakura Wars
games.source: Original production (concept by Oji Hiroi; characters by Kosuke Fujishima)
games.alsoOn: Windows, Dreamcast; remade on PS2 as Sakura Taisen: Atsuki Chishioni; PSP (Sakura Taisen 1&2)
games.cast: Akio Suyama (Ichiro Ogami), Chisa Yokoyama (Sakura Shinguji), Urara Takano, Michie Tomizawa, Kumiko Nishihara, Yuriko Fuchizaki, Mayumi Tanaka
games.cidTrigger: Opening theme "Geki! Teikoku Kagekidan" (Kohei Tanaka) and other vocal tracks may be registered with JASRAC
games.hook: Sega's biggest Japanese Saturn franchise: anime cutscenes, timed LIPS dialogue choices and steam-powered mech battles in a Taisho-era Tokyo theatre troupe.
games.video: Animated FMV opening and story cutscenes (anime by Kyokuichi Tokyo Movie/TMS, directed by Shunji Oga) plus CG segments by Buildup and Neverland — window size verify
games.difficulty: Easy to moderate; battles are forgiving
games.endings: Multiple endings, depending on which heroine Ogami grows closest to
games.trivia: Development took about three years, double the estimate. The anime cinematics came from Sega-owned Kyokuichi Tokyo Movie (later TMS), not Production I.G.
games.variants: First-print edition; Satakore budget reprint (verify); later Sakura Taisen Hanagumi Taisen and other spin-offs
games.notes: Japan-only, released September 1996 on two CDs. The official English name is Sakura Wars; an English fan translation exists. JP Saturn PriceCharting page not located.
games.criticSrc: average of 3 reviews on Wikipedia (Fam, RPGFan, Sega Saturn Magazine'' (JP))

games.title: Panzer Dragoon Saga
games.alt: Azel: Panzer Dragoon RPG (アゼル -パンツァードラグーン RPG-) (JP)
games.source: Original production; third Panzer Dragoon game
games.cast: Japanese voices: Akira Ishida (Edge), Maaya Sakamoto (Azel), Chikao Ohtsuka (Emperor)
games.hook: The holy grail of Saturn collecting: four discs of dragon-flight RPG whose source code was lost, so it has never been re-released.
games.cheats: Pandora's Box debug/extras menu, unlocked in late-game play (verify conditions)
games.video: Pre-rendered CG FMV cutscenes (full-screen letterboxed, verify), mixed with many real-time in-engine cutscenes
games.difficulty: Moderate; the real-time positional battle system is easy to learn
games.trivia: Sega published only a few thousand copies in the West. It was the highest-rated Saturn game on GameRankings. Its source code is said to be lost, which has blocked any port.
games.variants: JP Azel; NA and PAL Panzer Dragoon Saga (4-disc case)
games.notes: Fully voiced in Japanese with subtitles in all regions. Most storytelling is real-time, with pre-rendered CG for key scenes. Released JP January 1998, West April 1998.

games.title: Mega Man 8
games.alt: Rockman 8: Metal Heroes (ロックマン8 メタルヒーローズ) (JP)
games.alsoOn: PlayStation; PS version in Mega Man Legacy Collection 2 (PS4, Xbox One, Switch, PC)
games.cast: English dub voice cast (uncredited/verify); widely mocked for 'Dr. Wily' pronounced 'Dr. Wahwee'
games.hook: The Saturn version of Mega Man 8 has anime cutscenes, one of gaming's most infamous English dubs, and extra Cut Man and Wood Man boss fights the PS version lacks.
games.video: Animated FMV cutscenes by Xebec; small window
games.difficulty: Moderate; easier than the NES entries
games.trivia: Saturn exclusives: extra bosses Cut Man and Wood Man, a gallery of official and fan art, sound tests, a hidden cutscene viewer and a different Tengu Man stage theme.
games.variants: JP Rockman 8 Metal Heroes (17 Jan 1997; later Satakore reprint); NA Mega Man 8 (March 1997). No PAL Saturn release
games.modern: No (Saturn version); PS version in Mega Man Legacy Collection 2
games.notes: Wikipedia: localised for PS alone in PAL regions, so no PAL Saturn release. MobyGames Saturn scores not visible.

games.title: Mega Man X4
games.alsoOn: PlayStation, Windows; in Mega Man X Legacy Collection 2 (PS4, Xbox One, Switch, PC)
games.cast: English dub voice cast (verify)
games.cidTrigger: JP theme songs by Yukie Nakama ('Makenai Ai ga Kitto aru', 'One More Chance')
games.hook: Mega Man X4 has a dual X/Zero campaign with anime cutscenes, and on Saturn they are crunchier and slower to load than on PlayStation.
games.video: Animated FMV cutscenes by Xebec; Saturn's are lower quality than the PS versions
games.endings: Separate endings for X and Zero
games.trivia: X4 began as a Saturn exclusive slated for June 1997 before going multi-platform. Capcom's European distributor Virgin declined to release the Saturn version.
games.variants: JP Rockman X4 (1 August 1997; Special Limited Pack with Ultimate Armor X figure); NA Saturn early August 1997. No PAL Saturn release
games.modern: No (Saturn version); PS version in Mega Man X Legacy Collection 2
games.notes: Wikipedia: Europe got only the PS version (13 Oct 1997), so eu is false. MobyGames Saturn scores not visible.
games.criticSrc: average of 6 reviews on Wikipedia (EGM, GSpot, GameFan, GamePro, Saturn Power, Sega Saturn Magazine)

games.title: Mega Man X3
games.source: Port of the 1995 SNES game with added anime cutscenes and arranged CD music
games.alsoOn: SNES, PlayStation (JP/EU), Windows; SNES version in Mega Man X Legacy Collection
games.hook: The CD version of Mega Man X3 adds anime cutscenes and a remixed CD soundtrack, and it never came out in North America.
games.video: Animated FMV cutscenes added for the CD versions; small window (verify)
games.endings: Ending varies slightly depending on whether Zero survives (verify)
games.trivia: Capcom said it would license the 32-bit version to a US company, but it never came out in North America. Saturn Power named it the worst Saturn game.
games.variants: JP Rockman X3 (26 April 1996); PAL Mega Man X3 (March 1997). Never released in NA
games.modern: No (CD version); the SNES version is in Mega Man X Legacy Collection
games.notes: JP/EU only. EU publisher unconfirmed. No US PriceCharting page; priced from the JP Saturn page (Rockman X3).
games.criticSrc: average of 4 reviews on Wikipedia (Fam, GameFan, Saturn Power, Sega Saturn Magazine)

games.title: Lunar 2: Eternal Blue
games.alt: Lunar 2: Eternal Blue (LUNAR2 エターナルブルー) (JP Saturn); remake of Lunar: Eternal Blue (Mega-CD); PS version localised as Lunar 2: Eternal Blue Complete
games.developer: Game Arts (with Japan Art Media — verify)

games.hook: Lunar 2 on Saturn is the first release of the Eternal Blue remake, with roughly an hour of new anime cutscenes, and it came out a year before the PlayStation version.
games.video: Animated FMV cutscenes (new anime produced for the remake, reportedly by Studio Gonzo, verify)
games.difficulty: Moderate; easier than the Sega CD original
games.endings: Single ending; epilogue content after the ending
games.trivia: Released on Saturn in Japan on 23 July 1998; only the later PlayStation version (Complete) was localised, by Working Designs.
games.variants: Standard edition (2 CDs); limited edition — verify. The PS version (May 1999) was on 3 discs
games.notes: JP-only Saturn release, 23 July 1998, Kadokawa Shoten, two discs (ja Wikipedia). Anime studio for the remake unconfirmed (verify). JP Saturn PriceCharting page not located.

games.title: Pebble Beach Golf Links
games.alt: Pebble Beach Golf Links: Stadler Challenge (JP)
games.alsoOn: 3DO, SNES (True Golf: Pebble Beach / Pebble Beach no Hatou), PC-98, others in the series
games.cast: Craig Stadler (video guidance)
games.hook: An early Saturn golf game in which PGA pro Craig Stadler introduces each hole in live-action video.
games.video: Live-action FMV hole intros and tips from Craig Stadler in a small window; Cinepak (verify)
games.trivia: The 3DO original came first (1994); Sega published the Saturn version in 1995. Up to six players can play as digitised golfers.
games.notes: Stadler's guidance confirmed by Wikipedia; whether it is streamed video on Saturn and how much is unconfirmed (verify). Next Generation gave the Saturn version 3/5.
games.criticSrc: average of 14 reviews on Wikipedia (EGM, Electronic Entertainment, Fam, GI, GP, GamePro, Hyper, MAN!AC, NGen, Power Unlimited, Sega MegaZone, Sega Pro, The Electric Playground, VideoGames)

games.title: Space Hulk: Vengeance of the Blood Angels
games.developer: Krisalis Software (Saturn/PlayStation/PC versions; Key Game made the 3DO original)
games.source: Games Workshop Space Hulk / Warhammer 40,000 licence
games.cast: Unknown — verify
games.hook: Blood Angels Terminators fight Genestealers through a derelict hulk, with mission briefings in grim live-action and CG video.
games.video: FMV mission briefings and story cutscenes (live-action and CG) in a partial window (verify)
games.difficulty: Hard; real-time squad orders under pressure
games.trivia: The 3DO version came first (1995) and won 3DO Strategy/Puzzle Game of the Year; Saturn and PS ports followed.
games.variants: NA and PAL (JP release by EA Victor not confirmed, verify)
games.notes: Live-action/CG cutscene content is from memory of the 3DO version; Wikipedia does not describe the FMV, so its presence on Saturn is unconfirmed (verify). Sega Saturn Magazine praised the Saturn version.
games.criticSrc: average of 2 reviews on Wikipedia (Allgame, Sega Saturn Magazine)

games.title: Defcon 5
games.hook: A slow-burn, System Shock-style base-defence game: survive an alien attack on a deep-space mining base by running turrets, doors and air from VOS terminals.
games.video: Pre-rendered CG FMV intro and cinematic sequences, praised as well animated; whether the LIMO transit sequences are streamed — verify
games.difficulty: Hard; unclear objectives and lots of walking
games.endings: Escape with evidence; failure states otherwise (verify)
games.trivia: Released on Saturn in NA in December 1995 and PAL in June 1996. EGM's reviewers liked its story-driven approach; Sega Saturn Magazine panned it.
games.notes: Confirmed on Saturn (Wikipedia; PriceCharting has a US Saturn page). Title misuses DEFCON 5, which is actually peacetime readiness.
games.criticSrc: average of 2 reviews on Wikipedia (EGM, Sega Saturn Magazine)

games.title: Chaos Control
games.source: Original production (Infogrames; first released on CD-i/PC 1995)
games.alsoOn: CD-i (needs Digital Video Cartridge), DOS, Mac, PlayStation
games.peripherals: Standard pad; EU release supports light gun (Virtua Gun / Stunner)
games.hook: Infogrames' French sci-fi rail shooter: a crosshair over fully pre-rendered CG flythroughs of New York under alien attack, with heroine Jessica Darkhill.
games.video: Full-screen streamed pre-rendered CG with anime-style cutscenes and an overlaid crosshair
games.trivia: Lt. Jessica Darkhill fights the alien Kesh Rhan over Manhattan in 2050. GamePro named the CD-i version Best CD-i Game of 1995; Computer Gaming World later called the PC version the 38th-worst computer game ever.
games.variants: JP Saturn 1995 (pad only, no light gun); EU Saturn adds light gun and two-player; JP light-gun edition sold separately as Chaos Control Remix (1996)
games.notes: Wikipedia confirms Saturn releases in Japan (two versions) and Europe; no US Saturn release. JP original lacked light-gun support; the EU Chaos Control and JP Remix added it plus a two-player option. JP/EU publisher of the non-Remix Saturn version not confirmed.
games.criticSrc: Famitsu Cross Review on Japanese Wikipedia

games.title: Chaos Control Remix
games.alt: カオスコントロール リミックス
games.alsoOn: Saturn only (EU Chaos Control has the same light-gun features)
games.peripherals: Virtua Gun light gun supported; standard pad; two-player option
games.hook: Japan's light-gun edition of Chaos Control: shoot the CG flythroughs of alien-invaded Manhattan with the Virtua Gun, now with two players.
games.video: Full-screen streamed pre-rendered CG with anime-style cutscenes
games.trivia: Retitled Remix to avoid confusion with the previous year's Japanese release, which had no light-gun support. Sega Saturn Magazine (UK) gave it 56%, noting it can be finished in about half an hour.
games.variants: Japan only; matches the EU Saturn Chaos Control (light gun + two-player)
games.notes: Distinct JP Saturn SKU from the 1995 Chaos Control, confirmed by Wikipedia. Sega Saturn Magazine: polished rendering, monotonous play, very low longevity.
games.criticSrc: Famitsu Cross Review on Japanese Wikipedia

games.title: Mechanical Violator Hakaider: Last Judgement
games.alt: 人造人間ハカイダー ラストジャッジメント (Jinzou Ningen Hakaider: Last Judgement)
games.developer: Nihon Media Programming (game); video by Toei Video / Tohokushinsha
games.source: Sequel to the film Mechanical Violator Hakaider (1995, dir. Keita Amemiya, Toei/Tohokushinsha/Sega); new story by Toshiki Inoue
games.cast: Yuki Akimoto (Karen/Bijinder, live action), Jiro Okamoto (Hakaider suit actor); voices: Dai Matsumoto, Kazuhiko Inoue, Shinichiro Miki, Takeshi Watabe
games.cidTrigger: Toei film footage and score
games.hook: Sega's gun-game sequel to Keita Amemiya's grim 1995 tokusatsu film: ten years on, Hakaider returns to Jesus Town to win back his stolen right arm.
games.video: Streamed video sequences, including a live-action ending movie shot for the game (extent of in-game video unconfirmed)
games.trivia: Released 27 December 1996. The ending's live-action scenes were filmed specially, with then-newcomer Yuki Akimoto as Karen (Bijinder's human form). 'Last Judgement' was originally a proposed subtitle for the film. Kikaider villains Professor Gil and Waruder appear. A fan quality-of-life patch was released in April 2026 (SEGA Saturn Shiro).
games.notes: Saturn game confirmed by ja/en Wikipedia (film article, game section). Kept as a cutscene title: a newly shot live-action ending plus produced video; how much other video it streams is unconfirmed.

games.title: Segata Sanshiro Shinken Yuugi
games.alt: せがた三四郎 真剣遊戯 (Segata Sanshirou Shinken Yuugi)
games.source: Original production built on Sega's 1997–98 Segata Sanshiro TV ad campaign
games.cast: Hiroshi Fujioka (Segata Sanshiro)
games.cidTrigger: Segata Sanshiro theme song (Sega-owned; low risk)
games.hook: Hiroshi Fujioka's judo-throwing Saturn mascot stars in ten minigames whose reward is his run of live-action TV commercials, Sega's farewell to its most famous ad campaign.
games.video: Unlockable gallery of Segata's live-action TV commercials plus a music video; the ten minigames themselves are conventional (no streamed video shown in sources)
games.endings: Clear all ten minigames for a message from Segata and a music video
games.trivia: Released 29 October 1998. Minigames include Segata as Santa delivering presents and a Columns-style game where combos keep him from drowning. All 13 radio ads are playable in the 'Segata no Kotodama!!' mode. The campaign ended with Segata riding a missile into space to save Sega HQ.
games.notes: fmv lowered to 3: per Wikipedia, the live-action video is the unlockable commercials and music video, not the minigames. Gamers' Republic gave it an F; Hardcore Gaming 101 values it mostly as history.

games.title: Bakushou!! All Yoshimoto Quiz Ou Ketteisen DX
games.alt: 爆笑!!オール吉本クイズ王決定戦DX

games.cidTrigger: TV-style talent footage; possible TV music

games.video: Live-action video segments of comedians (verify)
games.trivia: Featured in Denfaminicogamer's survey of 1990s live-action games as a Saturn title.
games.notes: Saturn version is the DX edition (Sega Retro). The fetched reference pages were the wrong articles, so developer, cast and the amount of live-action video are still unconfirmed; fmv 6 is an estimate.

games.title: Soviet Strike
games.developer: Electronic Arts (Saturn version by Tiburon Entertainment)
games.cast: Live-action briefing cast (verify names)
games.hook: The Strike series goes 32-bit with live-action news reports and mission briefings between helicopter sorties.

games.trivia: Developed by EA's Strike team at the height of the series' popularity.
games.variants: NA, EU Saturn releases; JP unconfirmed (verify)
games.notes: Notable cutscene title; FMV is briefings and fake news. Critics praised the FMV acting (GameSpot: some of the best CD-ROM acting in a long time). Saturn version (1997) adds an easy mode, hidden weapons, analogue pad support and many bug fixes over the PS1. Sega Saturn Magazine Game of the Month. JP Saturn release unconfirmed.

games.title: Thunderhawk II
games.publisher: Core Design (EU/NA, verify NA), Victor Entertainment (JP)
games.source: Original production; sequel to Thunderhawk (Mega CD)
games.hook: Core Design's attack-helicopter sequel with FMV mission briefings and CG intros.
games.video: FMV briefings/cutscenes (verify live-action vs. CG)
games.trivia: Developed in parallel for PC, Saturn and PS1 on the original Thunderhawk engine; a playable PC build took a month. JP Saturn release by Victor on 23 February 1996 (product code T-6006G). GamesMaster ranked it 9th in its 1996 Saturn Top 10.
games.notes: Notable cutscene title; target release 4 December 1995 for all versions. Extent of FMV not described by Wikipedia.
games.criticSrc: average of 3 reviews on Wikipedia (EGM, Hyper, Sega Saturn Magazine)

games.title: Blazing Dragons
games.source: Original production by Terry Jones (Monty Python), later a TV cartoon

games.hook: Terry Jones' Monty Python-style Arthurian spoof with dragons as knights, in hand-drawn animation.
games.video: Animated cutscenes streamed from disc
games.trivia: Created by Terry Jones; became an animated TV series.
games.notes: Animated FMV cutscenes; fmv 3. Saturn/PS1 release by Crystal Dynamics in 1996 confirmed; fetched page was the TV series article, so the game's voice cast is unconfirmed.

games.title: Darkseed II
games.cast: Chris Gilbert (Mike Dawson); Japanese dub on Saturn
games.hook: H.R. Giger's biomechanical Dark World returns, with digitized actors walking pre-rendered sets.
games.video: Digitized actor animation and cutscenes (verify)
games.trivia: Sequel to Dark Seed, written by Raymond Benson with Twin Peaks influences; Giger licensed his art again. Saturn release 29 August 1997 in Japan, fully dubbed in Japanese; unlike the first game's Saturn port, no shuttle mouse support.
games.notes: Console versions were Japan-only and fully dubbed (Wikipedia). JP Saturn publisher unconfirmed. Mostly digitized actors over pre-rendered sets; may score lower. Famitsu: 'not for everyone'.
games.criticSrc: Famitsu Cross Review on Japanese Wikipedia

games.title: Ginga Eiyuu Densetsu
games.alt: 銀河英雄伝説 (Legend of the Galactic Heroes)
games.source: Anime/novel license: Legend of the Galactic Heroes (OVA)
games.alsoOn: PlayStation (1998); Saturn upgrade Ginga Eiyuu Densetsu Plus (1997)
games.cidTrigger: OVA footage and classical score

games.video: Anime movie clips from the OVA play at story events
games.endings: Follows the first five novels; events can diverge (e.g. the civil war's sides vary)
games.trivia: Released 6 December 1996. Closest to the PC Ginga Eiyuu Densetsu III: free galaxy-map invasion with real-time fleet battles. A mid-game civil war always breaks out, with admirals picking sides by affinity.
games.variants: Japan only; Plus (23 Oct 1997) adds anime-cast voices, a scenario mode and harder routes
games.notes: Saturn release and anime event movies confirmed by ja Wikipedia. Plus edition is a separate SKU not yet in the index.

games.title: Magic Knight Rayearth
games.cidTrigger: Anime opening footage and song
games.hook: The last US Saturn release (1998), Working Designs' long-delayed localization of Sega's CLAMP action RPG with anime cutscenes.
games.video: Anime FMV opening (Working Designs re-made it for the new English logo) and cutscenes
games.trivia: One of 12 Saturn games shown at the June 1994 Tokyo Toy Show; became the last US Saturn release in 1998. Working Designs rebuilt source code lost in a hard-drive crash and toughened the enemy AI.
games.variants: JP 1995; NA 1998 (standard and limited box with extras)
games.notes: Notable cutscene title. The US release replaced the Japanese theme 'Yuzurenai Negai' with English 'Daring Dreams'.
games.criticSrc: average of 9 reviews on Wikipedia (Ação Games, EGM, Fam, GI, GSpot, GameFan, Gamers, Sega Saturn Magazine'' (JP), Video Games)

games.title: Dragon's Lair
games.developer: Advanced Microcomputer Systems (Rick Dyer); animation by Don Bluth Productions
games.publisher: Cinematronics (NA); Atari (EU distribution, verify); JP distributor verify
games.source: Original production: hand-drawn animation by Don Bluth's studio for the game
games.alsoOn: Amiga, Atari ST, MS-DOS, Mac (ReadySoft floppy & CD-ROM), CD-i, Sega CD, 3DO, Jaguar CD, DVD and Blu-ray (Digital Leisure), Game Boy Color, iOS, Android, DSiWare, PS3, Wii and Switch (Dragon's Lair Trilogy), Steam, Arcade1Up cabinet; loose adaptations: Escape from Singe's Castle (C64/CPC/Spectrum), NES and SNES Dragon's Lair
games.cast: Dan Molina (Dirk's voice), Vera Lanpher (Daphne's vocals), Michael Rye (narrator)
games.peripherals: Upright cabinet, 4-way joystick + one Sword button; Pioneer PR-7820 (early units) or Pioneer LD-V1000; later Sony LDP replacement kits
games.cidTrigger: Digital Leisure owns the rights and has claimed footage uploads before (verify)
games.hook: The $0.50 cartoon that stopped 1983 arcades cold and one of the three video games held by the Smithsonian.
games.cheats: Operator DIP switches: lives, difficulty, unlimited lives / free play (exact switch numbers verify)
games.video: Full-screen hand-drawn animation from the disc, no overlays; the hardware just seeks to the next scene or a death clip
games.difficulty: Brutal: one wrong or late input kills Dirk, with no on-screen prompt beyond flashes of light
games.endings: One ending (Dirk rescues Daphne); scene order is randomised and some rooms play mirrored
games.trivia: Michael Rye's narrator and Dan Molina's Dirk were studio staff, not hired actors; cabinets famously needed constant laserdisc player repairs.
games.variants: Rev. F/F2 US ROMs; European Atari-built cabinet with different disc revision (verify); Dragon's Lair Enhancement 2.1 community ROM; conversion kits for Space Ace
games.modern: Yes (Digital Leisure DVD/Blu-ray, Steam, Dragon's Lair Trilogy on Switch/PS4/Xbox One, Arcade1Up 3-in-1 cabinet; emulated in Hypseus Singe/Daphne and MAME with the disc image; an arcade disc alone does nothing on a home LD player)

games.notes: Year: July 1, 1983 (Wikipedia). Moby page is pooled multi-platform with no arcade critic score.

games.title: Space Ace

games.alsoOn: Amiga, Apple IIGS, Atari ST, MS-DOS, Mac (ReadySoft), CD-i (1993), Sega CD (1994), 3DO, Jaguar CD, DVD and Blu-ray (Digital Leisure), iOS, Android, DSiWare, PS3, Wii and Switch (Dragon's Lair Trilogy), Steam, Arcade1Up; SNES (Absolute, 1994, a different action game)

games.title: Dragon's Lair II: Time Warp
games.source: Original Don Bluth animation, begun 1983 and finished about 1990 ($2.3M, three years of animation)
games.alsoOn: Amiga, Atari ST, MS-DOS (ReadySoft, 1990), CD-i (1994), Mac (1996), DVD (1998) and Blu-ray (2009) by Digital Leisure, DSiWare, PS3, iOS, Wii and Switch (Dragon's Lair Trilogy), Steam, Arcade1Up 3-in-1, Apple IIGS (Brutal Deluxe, 2022)

games.title: Cliff Hanger
games.developer: Stern Electronics (with Tokyo Movie Shinsha footage)
games.source: Repurposed anime: Lupin III films The Castle of Cagliostro (1979, Miyazaki) and The Mystery of Mamo (1978), TMS
games.cast: — (English dub voices; names not credited, verify)
games.peripherals: Upright cabinet; joystick + Hand and Feet buttons; Pioneer laserdisc player (PR-8210 / LD-V1000, verify)
